tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

content.content:
67	## The algorithm
68	
69	Mirrors RDT 2.4.0 (`lib/parser.js`). Method names are from the 7.1 client.
70	
71	1. `getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)`, then `getExportsOfModule`.
72	2. For each export, `getTypeOfSymbol`, then `getSignaturesOfType(Call)`. A component has a signature whose first parameter is named `props` or is the only parameter. For a class, use `Construct` signatures and read `props` from the instance type.
73	3. Props type: `getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(param, param.valueDeclaration)`. Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each member's when it is a union.
74	4. Per prop, `type` is `typeToString(getBaseConstraintOfType(t) ?? t)` with default flags, so long types truncate as they do in RDT. `required` means the symbol lacks `Optional` and has no code default.
75	5. `parent` is the first declaration's parent when that is an interface or type alias. `declarations` is every declaration's parent.
76	6. `description` and `tags` come from `getDocumentationComment` and `getJsDocTags`.
77	
78	RDT also emits any exported symbol that has a JSDoc comment but no props. We don't. In the fixture corpus, 23 of the 26 entries only RDT emits are of this kind, such as enum members, type aliases and functions.
79	
80	## TypeScript 7.1 API
81	
82	| Topic | Detail |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| Where | `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`7.1.0-dev`). typescript-go closed on 2026-08-20 |
85	| Timeline | Beta 2026-10-06, RC 2026-11-10, stable 2026-11-24 ([#63703](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703)) |
86	| Get it | `npm i typescript@next`. 7.0.x has no API |
87	| Launch | `tsc --api --async --cwd <dir>`: JSON-RPC with LSP-style `Content-Length` framing, handled concurrently. Without `--async`: msgpack over stdio, strictly serial. `--pipe` uses a socket |
88	| Stability | JS entry points are `typescript/unstable/*`. The protocol has no version handshake, so pin the build |
89	| Positions | UTF-16 code units. OXC offsets are UTF-8 bytes |
90	| Surface | 157 methods on 2026-09-19, mostly with TS 6 checker names |
91	
92	**Churn.** About 20 commits touched the protocol definition (`proto.go`) between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-18. `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params were reshaped on 09-17 and 09-18. Every call the algorithm uses ran unchanged on the 09-20 and 09-26 nightlies. Re-verify on the beta.
93	
94	**Freshness.** tsc sees an edit to a dependency only when told:
95	
96	```js
97	const s1 = await s0.update({ fileNotifications: { changed: [file] }, ensurePrograms: true })
98	```
99	
100	With the notification, the dependent component's props updated (0.5 ms update, 2.8 ms query). An unnotified disk edit stayed stale (2026-09-20).
101

## The algorithm

Mirrors RDT 2.4.0 (`lib/parser.js`). Method names are from the 7.1 client.

1. `getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)`, then `getExportsOfModule`.
2. For each export, `getTypeOfSymbol`, then `getSignaturesOfType(Call)`. A component has a signature whose first parameter is named `props` or is the only parameter. For a class, use `Construct` signatures and read `props` from the instance type.
3. Props type: `getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(param, param.valueDeclaration)`. Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each member's when it is a union.
4. Per prop, `type` is `typeToString(getBaseConstraintOfType(t) ?? t)` with default flags, so long types truncate as they do in RDT. `required` means the symbol lacks `Optional` and has no code default.
5. `parent` is the first declaration's parent when that is an interface or type alias. `declarations` is every declaration's parent.
6. `description` and `tags` come from `getDocumentationComment` and `getJsDocTags`.

RDT also emits any exported symbol that has a JSDoc comment but no props. We don't. In the fixture corpus, 23 of the 26 entries only RDT emits are of this kind, such as enum members, type aliases and functions.

## TypeScript 7.1 API

| Topic | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Where | `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`7.1.0-dev`). typescript-go closed on 2026-08-20 |
| Timeline | Beta 2026-10-06, RC 2026-11-10, stable 2026-11-24 ([#63703](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703)) |
| Get it | `npm i typescript@next`. 7.0.x has no API |
| Launch | `tsc --api --async --cwd <dir>`: JSON-RPC with LSP-style `Content-Length` framing, handled concurrently. Without `--async`: msgpack over stdio, strictly serial. `--pipe` uses a socket |
| Stability | JS entry points are `typescript/unstable/*`. The protocol has no version handshake, so pin the build |
| Positions | UTF-16 code units. OXC offsets are UTF-8 bytes |
| Surface | 157 methods on 2026-09-19, mostly with TS 6 checker names |

**Churn.** About 20 commits touched the protocol definition (`proto.go`) between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-18. `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params were reshaped on 09-17 and 09-18. Every call the algorithm uses ran unchanged on the 09-20 and 09-26 nightlies. Re-verify on the beta.

**Freshness.** tsc sees an edit to a dependency only when told:

```js
const s1 = await s0.update({ fileNotifications: { changed: [file] }, ensurePrograms: true })
```

With the notification, the dependent component's props updated (0.5 ms update, 2.8 ms query). An unnotified disk edit stayed stale (2026-09-20).

## Evidence

Method: RDT 2.4.0 on TypeScript 5.9.3 with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above on tsgo. The probe scripts are not in the repo yet.

| Check | Result | Nightly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13 components: the 10 outliers, base-ui `MenuRoot`, shadcn `Button`, mui `Button` | 0 missing and 0 extra props. `required` 3412/3412. Type strings 3410/3412 | 09-26 |
| Descriptions: ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 | 09-20 |
| `parent`: ariakit `MenuButton` | 294/294 in 12 requests | 09-20 |
| Fixture corpus, 55 files in one program | 70 components in common, equal prop counts on 70/70 | 09-20 |
| Class components | 2/2 on a synthetic file. The corpus has none | 09-20 |

Type strings match after two normalizations. tsc prints union members in internal type-id order, which differs from TS 5.9, so members are compared as a set. RDT also runs `.replace(' | undefined', '')` twice, which turns a nested `=> string | undefined` into `=> string` and loses information. Canonical output keeps it. The 2 remaining differences are nested `ref` unions in fluentui and base-ui.

Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have no props and 3 are default exports RDT names differently (mui `Button` confirmed at 311/311).

## Cost

Measured through the Node client on one macOS machine, so a Rust client should be lower.

| Measure | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Spawn and first snapshot | 33–72 ms |
| First checker query | 1–15 ms |
| Request round trip | 0.1 ms. 500 positions in one request take about 1 ms |
| 55-file corpus, one program | 385 ms and 937 requests. RDT in-process: 955 ms |
| Server memory | About 100 MB (MUI `Button`) |
| Structural path, for comparison | 50 ms for the whole corpus, 1.75–2.1 ms per incremental update (`docs/benchmarks.md`) |

Trimming the process, on the MUI `Button` query (median of 5 runs, 2026-09-20). Differences under about 10 ms are noise.

| Config                                 |   Wall |    CPU | Memory |
| -------------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | -----: |
| Default                                |  85 ms | 270 ms | 102 MB |
| `types: []`                            |  79 ms | 260 ms | 100 MB |
| `types: []`, `GOGC=off`                |  71 ms | 200 ms | 111 MB |
| `types: []`, `GOMAXPROCS=2`            | 114 ms | 160 ms |  99 MB |
| Default, plus 300 unrelated root files |  88 ms | 320 ms | 112 MB |

Pass only the files you need as roots. The API's checker is lazy, and diagnostics and emit never run.

## Boundaries

- **`crates/core`** owns the semantic result type, the merge and the diagnostics. It has no I/O, no async and no protocol types. The merge lives here because `OpaqueDetail` and `ParsedProp` internals are `pub(crate)`.
- **Backend crate** (feature-gated, off by default) spawns `tsc --api`, speaks the protocol, and handles timeouts and supervision. `config.rs` has none of these today.
- **CLI and NAPI** only switch it on. Neither calls JS.
- **Not a `DocgenPlugin`.** The hook is synchronous and runs on the cold path only. `WatchSession::update_file` skips plugins.
- **Failure** leaves the structural result and adds a diagnostic. It never fails extraction.
- **Determinism.** Reversing the query order changed no union order across 16 props in 3 files (2026-09-20). Whether canonical output sorts unions is open (below).

## Gates before it ships

| Gate | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Accuracy against RDT | Passed on 13 components. See not verified below |
| Lifecycle | Not started: missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification |
| Cost | Measured through the Node client. Repeat with the Rust client |
| Determinism | Clean and incremental runs must produce the same output |
| Oracle | Broken. See below |

## The RDT oracle is broken

`apps/validate` depends on `typescript ^7.0.2`, and RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined). The baselines on disk date from 2026-07-25. RDT needs a TypeScript 6 API: `typescript@6`, or `@typescript/typescript6` from the 7.0 announcement.

The harness also compares only name, `required`, type and default, and renders our types itself in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`). Its type mismatches mix resolver and renderer differences, and description, `parent` and `declarations` are never compared.

## Open decisions

1. **Output type.** Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly: `Named` has no file or symbol, `EventHandler` has no return type, `Tuple` has no optional or rest elements, and `Object` has no index signatures. Add a variant or map into existing ones. `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version, so add one first.
2. **`ref` and `key`.** RDT emits both, and nothing else records forwardRef metadata. Semantic mode must match whatever the structural path does.
3. **Trigger.** Run on every exported component or only on files with degrade diagnostics. Bare generic parameters and TypeScript utility types resolve to `Named` with no diagnostic by design, so the second misses them.
4. **Union order.** Sort in canonical output, or keep source order for structural results.

## Not verified

- A Rust client. Every measurement uses the Node client.
- Overloads with more than one signature, static sub-components (`Menu.Item`), and barrel re-exports, where RDT names components by the barrel file.
- `@default` and `@type` JSDoc overrides.
- Projects larger than the 55-file corpus.
- What the `MappedType` accessors added on 2026-09-23 ([#64397](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64397)) expose beyond resolved properties.

1	import * as path from 'node:path'
2	import { withCustomConfig } from 'react-docgen-typescript'
3	import { discoverFixtures, FIXTURES_ROOT } from './fixtures.ts'
4	import type { ToolResult } from './types.ts'
5	
6	const tsconfigPath = path.resolve(FIXTURES_ROOT, '..', 'tsconfig.json')
7	
8	// Falls back to a minimal option set if the extended options throw for this tsconfig.
9	function makeParser() {
10	  try {
11	    return withCustomConfig(tsconfigPath, {
12	      shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum: true,
13	      shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional: true,
14	      propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false },
15	    })
16	  } catch {
17	    return withCustomConfig(tsconfigPath, { shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum: true })
18	  }
19	}
20	
21	// react-docgen-typescript represents union/literal prop types as
22	// `{ name: 'enum', value: [{ value: '"foo"' }, ...] }` (with
23	// shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum) instead of putting the real type string
24	// in `.name` — reading `.name` alone for these props compares the literal
25	// string "enum" against our real union string, which isn't a type
26	// difference, it's reading the wrong field.
27	function rdtTypeToString(type: { name?: string; value?: Array<{ value: string }> } | undefined): string {
28	  if (!type) return 'unknown'
29	  if (type.name === 'enum' && Array.isArray(type.value)) {
30	    return type.value.map((v) => v.value).join(' | ')
31	  }
32	  return type.name ?? 'unknown'
33	}
34	
35	const parser = makeParser()
36	const fixtures = discoverFixtures().filter((f) => !f.isDts) // RDT needs real TS files
37	const results: ToolResult[] = []
38	
39	for (const fixture of fixtures) {
40	  const start = performance.now()
41	  try {
42	    const raw = parser.parse(fixture.path)
43	    const durationMs = performance.now() - start
44	    // One entry per component so keys match our tool's ${lib}/${basename}/${displayName} format.
45	    for (const comp of raw) {
46	      results.push({
47	        tool: 'react-docgen-typescript',
48	        fixture: `${fixture.name}/${comp.displayName}`,
49	        durationMs,
50	        output: {
51	          [comp.displayName]: {
52	            displayName: comp.displayName,
53	            description: comp.description ?? '',
54	            props: Object.fromEntries(
55	              Object.entries(comp.props ?? {}).map(([propName, prop]: [string, any]) => [
56	                propName,
57	                {
58	                  name: propName,
59	                  required: prop.required ?? false,
60	                  type: rdtTypeToString(prop.type),
61	                  description: prop.description ?? '',
62	                  defaultValue: prop.defaultValue?.value,
63	                },
64	              ]),
65	            ),
66	          },
67	        },
68	      })
69	    }
70	    if (raw.length === 0) {
71	      results.push({
72	        tool: 'react-docgen-typescript',
73	        fixture: fixture.name,
74	        durationMs,
75	        output: {},
76	        error: 'no components found',
77	      })
78	    }
79	  } catch (error: any) {
80	    results.push({
81	      tool: 'react-docgen-typescript',
82	      fixture: fixture.name,
83	      durationMs: performance.now() - start,
84	      output: {},
85	      error: error.message,
86	    })
87	  }
88	}
89	
90	console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2))

1	import { resolve } from 'node:path'
2	import { readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
3	
4	export const FIXTURES_ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '../../../fixtures')
5	
6	export interface Fixture {
7	  name: string // e.g. "shadcn/button"
8	  path: string // absolute path
9	  ext: string // ".tsx" | ".ts" | ".d.ts"
10	  isTsx: boolean
11	  isDts: boolean
12	}
13	
14	export function discoverFixtures(): Fixture[] {
15	  const fixtures: Fixture[] = []
16	  for (const dir of readdirSync(FIXTURES_ROOT)) {
17	    const dirPath = resolve(FIXTURES_ROOT, dir)
18	    if (!statSync(dirPath).isDirectory()) continue
19	    if (dir === 'panda') continue // skip styled-system subdir complexity for now
20	    for (const file of readdirSync(dirPath)) {
21	      if (!file.endsWith('.ts') && !file.endsWith('.tsx')) continue
22	      if (file === 'index.ts') continue // skip barrel files for now
23	      let ext = '.ts'
24	      if (file.endsWith('.d.ts')) ext = '.d.ts'
25	      else if (file.endsWith('.tsx')) ext = '.tsx'
26	      fixtures.push({
27	        name: `${dir}/${file.replace(/\.tsx?$/, '').replace(/\.d$/, '')}`,
28	        path: resolve(dirPath, file),
29	        ext,
30	        isTsx: file.endsWith('.tsx'),
31	        isDts: file.endsWith('.d.ts'),
32	      })
33	    }
34	  }
35	  return fixtures.toSorted((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))
36	}

1	import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs'
2	import type { ToolResult } from './types.ts'
3	
4	function loadBaseline(name: string): Map<string, ToolResult> | null {
5	  const p = `./baselines/${name}.json`
6	  if (!existsSync(p)) return null
7	  const results: ToolResult[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8'))
8	  return new Map(results.map((r) => [r.fixture, r]))
9	}
10	
11	const rdg = loadBaseline('react-docgen')
12	const rdt = loadBaseline('react-docgen-typescript')
13	const ours = loadBaseline('oxc-react-docgen')
14	
15	if (!rdg && !rdt && !ours) {
16	  console.error('No baselines found. Run at least one tool first.')
17	  process.exit(1)
18	}
19	
20	const allFixtures = new Set([
21	  ...(rdg ? [...rdg.keys()] : []),
22	  ...(rdt ? [...rdt.keys()] : []),
23	  ...(ours ? [...ours.keys()] : []),
24	])
25	
26	let totalOwn = 0,
27	  rdtTotal = 0,
28	  oursTotal = 0,
29	  wins = 0,
30	  ties = 0,
31	  misses = 0
32	
33	for (const fixture of [...allFixtures].toSorted()) {
34	  const r_rdg = rdg?.get(fixture)
35	  const r_rdt = rdt?.get(fixture)
36	  const r_ours = ours?.get(fixture)
37	
38	  console.log(`\n## ${fixture}`)
39	
40	  if (r_rdg?.error) console.log(`  ❌ react-docgen: ${r_rdg.error.slice(0, 100)}`)
41	  if (r_rdt?.error) console.log(`  ❌ react-docgen-typescript: ${r_rdt.error.slice(0, 100)}`)
42	  if (r_ours?.error) console.log(`  ❌ oxc-react-docgen: ${r_ours.error.slice(0, 100)}`)
43	
44	  const times: string[] = []
45	  if (r_rdg) times.push(`rdg: ${r_rdg.durationMs.toFixed(1)}ms`)
46	  if (r_rdt) times.push(`rdt: ${r_rdt.durationMs.toFixed(1)}ms`)
47	  if (r_ours) times.push(`ours: ${r_ours.durationMs.toFixed(1)}ms`)
48	  if (times.length > 0) console.log(`  ⏱  ${times.join('  |  ')}`)
49	
50	  const rdgComps = Object.keys(r_rdg?.output ?? {})
51	  const rdtComps = Object.keys(r_rdt?.output ?? {})
52	  const oursComps = Object.keys(r_ours?.output ?? {})
53	  const allComps = new Set([...rdgComps, ...rdtComps, ...oursComps])
54	
55	  for (const comp of [...allComps].toSorted()) {
56	    const rdgProps = Object.keys(r_rdg?.output?.[comp]?.props ?? {})
57	    const rdtProps = Object.keys(r_rdt?.output?.[comp]?.props ?? {})
58	    const oursProps = Object.keys(r_ours?.output?.[comp]?.props ?? {})
59	
60	    console.log(`\n  ### ${comp}`)
61	    console.log(`    props: rdg=${rdgProps.length}  rdt=${rdtProps.length}  ours=${oursProps.length}`)
62	
63	    rdtTotal += rdtProps.length
64	    oursTotal += oursProps.length
65	
66	    // Props ours has that rdt doesn't
67	    const oursOnly = oursProps.filter((p) => !rdtProps.includes(p))
68	    const rdtOnly = rdtProps.filter((p) => !oursProps.includes(p))
69	    const rdgOnly = rdgProps.filter((p) => !oursProps.includes(p))
70	    const common = oursProps.filter((p) => rdtProps.includes(p))
71	    const ourInheritedElements = r_ours?.inheritedElements ?? []
72	
73	    if (oursOnly.length > 0) console.log(`    ours-only (${oursOnly.length}): ${oursOnly.slice(0, 8).join(', ')}`)
74	    if (rdgOnly.length > 0)
75	      console.log(
76	        `    rdg-only  (${rdgOnly.length}): ${rdgOnly.slice(0, 5).join(', ')}${rdgOnly.length > 5 ? '...' : ''}`,
77	      )
78	
79	    // For rdt-only props: distinguish HTML attrs covered by our notableInherited from true misses.
80	    // We trust our notableInherited list as the ground truth for what we surface from HTML elements.
81	    const ourNotableNames = new Set(r_ours?.notableInheritedNames)
82	    if (rdtOnly.length > 0) {
83	      // A prop is "covered by our inheritance" if it appears in our notableInherited list.
84	      // Props not in notableInherited and not in our own props are true misses.
85	      const coveredByInheritance = rdtOnly.filter((p) => ourNotableNames.has(p))
86	      const trueMisses = rdtOnly.filter((p) => !ourNotableNames.has(p) && !oursProps.includes(p))
87	      if (trueMisses.length > 0) {
88	        console.log(`    ❗ rdt-only REAL MISSES (${trueMisses.length}): ${trueMisses.slice(0, 8).join(', ')}`)
89	        misses += trueMisses.length
90	      }
91	      if (coveredByInheritance.length > 0) {
92	        console.log(`    ℹ️  rdt expands ${coveredByInheritance.length} attrs we surface via notableInherited`)
93	      }
94	      const unexpandedHtmlAttrs = rdtOnly.filter(
95	        (p) => !ourNotableNames.has(p) && !oursProps.includes(p) && /^(on[A-Z]|aria-|data-)/.test(p),
96	      )
97	      if (unexpandedHtmlAttrs.length > 0 && ourInheritedElements.length > 0) {
98	        console.log(
99	          `    ℹ️  ${unexpandedHtmlAttrs.length} additional HTML event/ARIA attrs rdt expands (not in our notableInherited)`,
100	        )
101	      }
102	    }
103	
104	    // Type comparison (ours vs rdt)
105	    const typeDiffs = common
106	      .filter((p) => {
107	        const o = r_ours?.output?.[comp]?.props?.[p]?.type
108	        const t = r_rdt?.output?.[comp]?.props?.[p]?.type
109	        return o && t && o !== t
110	      })
111	      .map((p) => ({
112	        prop: p,
113	        ours: r_ours?.output?.[comp]?.props?.[p]?.type ?? '?',
114	        rdt: r_rdt?.output?.[comp]?.props?.[p]?.type ?? '?',
115	      }))
116	
117	    if (typeDiffs.length > 0) {
118	      console.log(`    type diffs (${typeDiffs.length}):`)
119	      for (const d of typeDiffs.slice(0, 5)) {
120	        console.log(`      ${d.prop}: ours="${d.ours}"  rdt="${d.rdt}"`)
121	      }
122	    }
123	
124	    // A win is: no real misses, no unexpected extra props, no type diffs, and we found something.
125	    const rdtOnlyRealCount = rdtOnly.filter((p) => !ourNotableNames.has(p) && !oursProps.includes(p)).length
126	
127	    if (oursOnly.length === 0 && rdtOnlyRealCount === 0 && typeDiffs.length === 0 && oursProps.length > 0) {
128	      console.log(`    ✅ own props match rdt`)
129	      wins++
130	    } else if (oursProps.length === 0 && rdtProps.length === 0) {
131	      ties++
132	    } else if (oursProps.length === 0 && rdtProps.length > 0 && ourInheritedElements.length > 0) {
133	      const notableCount = ourNotableNames.size
134	      const rdtCovered = rdtOnly.filter((p) => ourNotableNames.has(p)).length
135	      if (rdtCovered === rdtProps.length) {
136	        console.log(`    ✅ 0 own props, all ${rdtProps.length} rdt props covered by notableInherited`)
137	        wins++
138	      } else {
139	        console.log(
140	          `    ⚠️  0 own props; we surface ${notableCount} notableInherited, rdt has ${rdtProps.length} total (inherits ${ourInheritedElements.join(', ')})`,
141	        )
142	      }
143	    } else if (oursProps.length === 0 && rdtProps.length > 0 && ourInheritedElements.length === 0) {
144	      console.log(`    ❌ ours found nothing, rdt found ${rdtProps.length} props`)
145	    }
146	
147	    totalOwn += oursProps.length
148	  }
149	}
150	
151	console.log(`\n${'='.repeat(60)}`)
152	console.log('SUMMARY')
153	console.log('='.repeat(60))
154	if (rdt) console.log(`react-docgen-typescript: ${rdtTotal} total props across all components`)
155	if (ours) console.log(`oxc-react-docgen:        ${oursTotal} total props across all components`)
156	console.log(`Coverage: ${oursTotal}/${rdtTotal} (${Math.round((oursTotal / Math.max(rdtTotal, 1)) * 100)}%)`)
157	console.log(`Identical matches: ${wins}  |  Both empty: ${ties}  |  Misses: ${misses}`)

1	import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
2	import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
3	import { resolve } from 'node:path'
4	
5	mkdirSync('./baselines', { recursive: true })
6	
7	function runScript(script: string): string {
8	  const result = spawnSync('tsx', [resolve(import.meta.dirname, script)], {
9	    encoding: 'utf8',
10	    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'inherit'], // stdout captured, stderr forwarded
11	    // Node's spawnSync default maxBuffer is 1MB — with 20 real fixture libraries
12	    // the RDT baseline alone now exceeds that, silently truncating stdout
13	    // mid-JSON-string (no non-zero exit, no thrown error) rather than failing
14	    // loudly. 100MB is generous headroom for however large fixtures/ grows.
15	    maxBuffer: 100 * 1024 * 1024,
16	  })
17	  if (result.error) throw new Error(`${script} failed to spawn: ${result.error.message}`)
18	  if (result.status !== 0) throw new Error(`${script} exited with status ${result.status}`)
19	  return result.stdout
20	}
21	
22	console.log('Running react-docgen baseline...')
23	writeFileSync('./baselines/react-docgen.json', runScript('run-react-docgen.ts'))
24	console.log('✅ react-docgen baseline saved')
25	
26	console.log('Running react-docgen-typescript baseline...')
27	writeFileSync('./baselines/react-docgen-typescript.json', runScript('run-react-docgen-typescript.ts'))
28	console.log('✅ react-docgen-typescript baseline saved')
29	
30	console.log('Running oxc-react-docgen baseline (html-attributes=full, fair vs RDT)...')
31	writeFileSync('./baselines/oxc-react-docgen.json', runScript('run-ours.ts'))
32	console.log('✅ oxc-react-docgen baseline saved')
33	
34	// react-docgen resolves zero `extends`/inherited-interface props of its own — comparing
35	// our html-attributes=full output (hundreds of synthesized inherited attrs per component)
36	// against it would manufacture a huge "extra in ours" count that's really just a
37	// no-inheritance-resolution-at-all vs some-resolution mismatch, not a real quality gap.
38	// A separate html-attributes=none baseline is the fair apples-to-apples comparator here.
39	console.log('Running oxc-react-docgen baseline (html-attributes=none, fair vs react-docgen)...')
40	process.env.HTML_ATTRIBUTES_MODE = 'none'

content.content:
1	import { readFileSync, existsSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
2	import type { ToolResult, NormalizedProp } from './types.ts'
3	
4	// ─── Loading ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5	
6	function loadBaseline(name: string): Map<string, ToolResult> | null {
7	  const p = `./baselines/${name}.json`
8	  if (!existsSync(p)) return null
9	  const results: ToolResult[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8'))
10	  return new Map(results.map((r) => [r.fixture, r]))
11	}
12	
13	const ours = loadBaseline('oxc-react-docgen')
14	// react-docgen resolves no inherited/`extends` props of its own — compare against our
15	// html-attributes=none baseline (falls back to the full baseline if that variant wasn't
16	// generated) so this pair isn't dominated by an inheritance-resolution mismatch instead of
17	// an actual prop-level agreement signal.
18	const oursForRdg = loadBaseline('oxc-react-docgen-none') ?? ours
19	const rdt = loadBaseline('react-docgen-typescript')
20	const rdg = loadBaseline('react-docgen')
21	
22	if (!ours) {
23	  console.error('No oxc-react-docgen baseline found — run `pnpm run:ours` first.')
24	  process.exit(1)
25	}
26	
27	// ─── Divergence taxonomy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
28	//
29	// Classifies a (ours, comparator) type-string mismatch into a bucket by
30	// observable shape only — it can't see root cause, just the diff. Root
31	// causes for the recurring buckets are cross-referenced in docs/benchmarks.md
32	// against docs/rdt-coverage.md's already-investigated gap list.
33	
34	type TypeDiffBucket =
35	  | 'cosmetic-formatting'
36	  | 'literal-narrowed-vs-widened'
37	  | 'union-member-order'
38	  | 'optional-undefined-representation'
39	  | 'structural-type-difference'
40	
41	function normalizeTypeString(s: string): string {
42	  return s.replaceAll(/\s+/g, ' ').replaceAll('"', "'").trim()
43	}
44	
45	function stripUndefinedMember(s: string): string {
46	  return s
47	    .split('|')
48	    .map((m) => m.trim())
49	    .filter((m) => m !== 'undefined')
50	    .join(' | ')
51	}
52	
53	function isLiteralish(s: string): boolean {
54	  return /^['"]/.test(s.trim()) || s.includes('|')
55	}
56	
57	const WIDENED = new Set(['string', 'number', 'boolean', 'unknown', 'any'])
58	
59	function classifyTypeDiff(oursType: string, otherType: string): TypeDiffBucket {
60	  if (normalizeTypeString(oursType) === normalizeTypeString(otherType)) return 'cosmetic-formatting'
61	
62	  if (stripUndefinedMember(oursType) === stripUndefinedMember(otherType) && oursType !== otherType) {
63	    return 'optional-undefined-representation'
64	  }
65	
66	  const oursMembers = oursType.split('|').map((m) => m.trim())
67	  const otherMembers = otherType.split('|').map((m) => m.trim())
68	  if (
69	    oursMembers.length > 1 &&
70	    oursMembers.length === otherMembers.length &&
71	    new Set(oursMembers).size === oursMembers.length &&
72	    [...oursMembers].toSorted().join('|') === [...otherMembers].toSorted().join('|') &&
73	    oursType !== otherType
74	  ) {
75	    return 'union-member-order'
76	  }
77	
78	  if (
79	    (WIDENED.has(otherType.trim()) && isLiteralish(oursType)) ||
80	    (WIDENED.has(oursType.trim()) && isLiteralish(otherType))
81	  ) {
82	    return 'literal-narrowed-vs-widened'
83	  }
84	
85	  return 'structural-type-difference'
86	}
87	
88	// ─── Per-pair agreement computation ──────────────────────────────────────
89	
90	interface PropDiff {
91	  fixture: string
92	  component: string
93	  prop: string
94	  kind: 'type-mismatch' | 'required-mismatch' | 'default-mismatch' | 'missing-in-ours' | 'extra-in-ours'
95	  bucket?: TypeDiffBucket
96	  ours?: string
97	  other?: string
98	  htmlInheritanceCovered?: boolean
99	}
100	
101	interface PairSummary {
102	  comparator: 'react-docgen-typescript' | 'react-docgen'
103	  componentsCompared: number
104	  /** Components where the comparator returned zero props at all — relevant for
105	   *  react-docgen specifically, which has weak native support for interface-typed
106	   *  (non-PropTypes) TypeScript components and frequently returns nothing. A flat
107	   *  per-prop agreement rate is close to meaningless when this is high; the more
108	   *  honest number is "how many real components does each tool find props for at all." */
109	  componentsWithEmptyComparatorOutput: number
110	  propsUnion: number
111	  matched: number
112	  mismatched: number
113	  missingInOurs: number
114	  missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered: number
115	  extraInOurs: number
116	  /** matched / (propsUnion - missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered) — the honest denominator excludes
117	   *  props we intentionally surface a different way (curated HTML-attribute inheritance) rather
118	   *  than pretending those never existed. */
119	  agreementRate: number
120	  typeDiffBuckets: Record<TypeDiffBucket, number>
121	  diffs: PropDiff[]
122	}
123	
124	function comparePair(
125	  oursMap: Map<string, ToolResult>,
126	  otherMap: Map<string, ToolResult>,
127	  comparatorName: 'react-docgen-typescript' | 'react-docgen',
128	): PairSummary {
129	  const summary: PairSummary = {
130	    comparator: comparatorName,
131	    componentsCompared: 0,
132	    componentsWithEmptyComparatorOutput: 0,
133	    propsUnion: 0,
134	    matched: 0,
135	    mismatched: 0,
136	    missingInOurs: 0,
137	    missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered: 0,
138	    extraInOurs: 0,
139	    agreementRate: 0,
140	    typeDiffBuckets: {
141	      'cosmetic-formatting': 0,
142	      'literal-narrowed-vs-widened': 0,
143	      'union-member-order': 0,
144	      'optional-undefined-representation': 0,
145	      'structural-type-difference': 0,
146	    },
147	    diffs: [],
148	  }
149	
150	  for (const [key, ourResult] of oursMap) {
151	    const otherResult = otherMap.get(key)
152	    if (!otherResult || ourResult.error || otherResult.error) continue
153	
154	    const fixture = key.split('/').slice(0, -1).join('/')
155	    const component = key.split('/').at(-1) ?? key
156	    const [ourComp] = Object.values(ourResult.output)
157	    const [otherComp] = Object.values(otherResult.output)
158	    if (!ourComp || !otherComp) continue
159	
160	    summary.componentsCompared++
161	    if (Object.keys(otherComp.props).length === 0) summary.componentsWithEmptyComparatorOutput++
162	    const notableInherited = new Set(ourResult.notableInheritedNames)
163	    const allPropNames = new Set([...Object.keys(ourComp.props), ...Object.keys(otherComp.props)])
164	
165	    for (const propName of allPropNames) {
166	      const op: NormalizedProp | undefined = ourComp.props[propName]
167	      const cp: NormalizedProp | undefined = otherComp.props[propName]
168	
169	      if (op && !cp) {
170	        summary.propsUnion++
171	        summary.extraInOurs++
172	        summary.diffs.push({ fixture, component, prop: propName, kind: 'extra-in-ours', ours: op.type })
173	        continue
174	      }
175	      if (!op && cp) {
176	        summary.propsUnion++
177	        if (notableInherited.has(propName)) {
178	          summary.missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered++
179	          summary.diffs.push({
180	            fixture,
181	            component,
182	            prop: propName,
183	            kind: 'missing-in-ours',
184	            other: cp.type,
185	            htmlInheritanceCovered: true,
186	          })
187	        } else {
188	          summary.missingInOurs++
189	          summary.diffs.push({ fixture, component, prop: propName, kind: 'missing-in-ours', other: cp.type })
190	        }
191	        continue
192	      }
193	      if (!op || !cp) continue // unreachable, both branches above cover the single-sided cases
194	
195	      summary.propsUnion++
196	      if (op.required !== cp.required) {
197	        summary.mismatched++
198	        summary.diffs.push({
199	          fixture,
200	          component,
201	          prop: propName,
202	          kind: 'required-mismatch',
203	          ours: String(op.required),
204	          other: String(cp.required),
205	        })
206	      } else if (op.type !== cp.type) {
207	        const bucket = classifyTypeDiff(op.type, cp.type)
208	        summary.typeDiffBuckets[bucket]++
209	        if (bucket === 'cosmetic-formatting') {
210	          summary.matched++
211	        } else {
212	          summary.mismatched++
213	          summary.diffs.push({
214	            fixture,
215	            component,
216	            prop: propName,
217	            kind: 'type-mismatch',
218	            bucket,
219	            ours: op.type,
220	            other: cp.type,
221	          })
222	        }
223	      } else if ((op.defaultValue ?? null) === (cp.defaultValue ?? null)) {
224	        summary.matched++
225	      } else {
226	        summary.mismatched++
227	        summary.diffs.push({
228	          fixture,
229	          component,
230	          prop: propName,
231	          kind: 'default-mismatch',
232	          ours: op.defaultValue,
233	          other: cp.defaultValue,
234	        })
235	      }
236	    }
237	  }
238	
239	  const honestDenominator = summary.propsUnion - summary.missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered
240	  summary.agreementRate = honestDenominator > 0 ? summary.matched / honestDenominator : 1
241	
242	  return summary
243	}
244	
245	// ─── Run ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
246	
247	const results: { generatedAt: string; pairs: PairSummary[] } = {
248	  generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
249	  pairs: [],
250	}
251	
252	if (rdt) results.pairs.push(comparePair(ours, rdt, 'react-docgen-typescript'))
253	if (rdg) results.pairs.push(comparePair(oursForRdg, rdg, 'react-docgen'))
254	
255	writeFileSync('./analysis.json', JSON.stringify(results, null, 2))
256	
257	for (const pair of results.pairs) {
258	  console.log(`\n${'='.repeat(70)}`)
259	  console.log(`ours vs ${pair.comparator}`)
260	  console.log('='.repeat(70))
261	  console.log(`Components compared: ${pair.componentsCompared}`)
262	  if (pair.componentsWithEmptyComparatorOutput > 0) {
263	    console.log(
264	      `  ⚠️  ${pair.comparator} returned ZERO props for ${pair.componentsWithEmptyComparatorOutput}/${pair.componentsCompared} of these components — a per-prop agreement rate is a weak signal when this is high; see docs/benchmarks.md.`,
265	    )
266	  }
267	  console.log(`Props in union:      ${pair.propsUnion}`)
268	  console.log(`  matched:                          ${pair.matched}`)
269	  console.log(`  mismatched (real):                ${pair.mismatched}`)
270	  console.log(`  missing in ours (real miss):       ${pair.missingInOurs}`)
271	  console.log(`  missing in ours (HTML-inherited):  ${pair.missingButHtmlInheritanceCovered}`)
272	  console.log(`  extra in ours:                     ${pair.extraInOurs}`)
273	  console.log(`Agreement rate (excl. HTML-inheritance design difference): ${(pair.agreementRate * 100).toFixed(1)}%`)
274	  console.log('Type-diff taxonomy (excluding cosmetic-formatting, which counts as matched):')
275	  for (const [bucket, count] of Object.entries(pair.typeDiffBuckets)) {
276	    if (bucket !== 'cosmetic-formatting' && count > 0) console.log(`  ${bucket}: ${count}`)
277	  }
278	}
279	
280	console.log(`\nFull structured output written to apps/validate/analysis.json`)

1	import { readFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs'
2	import type { ToolResult } from './types.ts'
3	
4	// Checks that the tsc-api algorithm in run-semantic.ts reproduces real RDT's output —
5	// the "Evidence" section of docs/type-checker-integration.md. This is a parity check
6	// between two implementations of the same algorithm, not a quality comparison (that's
7	// compare.ts/analyze.ts, which weigh oxc-react-docgen's structural resolver against RDT).
8	
9	function loadBaseline(name: string): Map<string, ToolResult> {
10	  const p = `./baselines/${name}.json`
11	  if (!existsSync(p)) {
12	    console.error(`Missing ./baselines/${name}.json — run \`pnpm baseline\` first.`)
13	    process.exit(1)
14	  }
15	  const results: ToolResult[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8'))
16	  return new Map(results.map((r) => [r.fixture, r]))
17	}
18	
19	// The rdt baseline's type strings are RDT's real output, already run through RDT's own
20	// `.replace(' | undefined', '')` twice (see docs/type-checker-integration.md, "Evidence")
21	// — lossy (`=> string | undefined` becomes `=> string`), but it's what RDT actually
22	// emits. Our canonical algorithm intentionally keeps `| undefined`, so replicate RDT's
23	// quirk on our side for this comparison only, rather than "fixing" RDT's already-baked
24	// output (which would under-strip: RDT applies the replace unconditionally, twice, no
25	// matter how many `| undefined` occurrences exist).
26	function applyRdtUndefinedQuirk(s: string): string {
27	  return s.replace(' | undefined', '').replace(' | undefined', '')
28	}
29	
30	// tsc prints union members in internal type-id order, which differs from TS 5.9's
31	// (RDT's) order, so members are compared as a set rather than a verbatim string.
32	function typesMatch(oursRawType: string, rdtType: string): boolean {
33	  const oursType = applyRdtUndefinedQuirk(oursRawType)
34	  if (oursType === rdtType) return true
35	  const a = oursType.split('|').map((m) => m.trim())
36	  const b = rdtType.split('|').map((m) => m.trim())
37	  return a.length > 1 && a.length === b.length && new Set(a).size === new Set([...a, ...b]).size
38	}
39	
40	const rdt = loadBaseline('react-docgen-typescript')
41	const semantic = loadBaseline('semantic')
42	
43	let componentsCompared = 0
44	let propsUnion = 0
45	let missing = 0
46	let extra = 0
47	let requiredMatched = 0
48	let requiredTotal = 0
49	let typeMatched = 0
50	let typeTotal = 0
51	let descriptionMatched = 0
52	let descriptionTotal = 0
53	const mismatches: string[] = []
54	
55	for (const [key, rdtResult] of rdt) {
56	  const semanticResult = semantic.get(key)
57	  if (!semanticResult || rdtResult.error || semanticResult.error) continue
58	
59	  const [rdtComp] = Object.values(rdtResult.output)
60	  const [semanticComp] = Object.values(semanticResult.output)
61	  if (!rdtComp || !semanticComp) continue
62	
63	  componentsCompared++
64	  descriptionTotal++
65	  if (rdtComp.description.trim() === semanticComp.description.trim()) descriptionMatched++
66	  else mismatches.push(`${key}: description differs`)
67	
68	  const allPropNames = new Set([...Object.keys(rdtComp.props), ...Object.keys(semanticComp.props)])
69	  for (const propName of allPropNames) {
70	    const rp = rdtComp.props[propName]
71	    const sp = semanticComp.props[propName]
72	    propsUnion++
73	
74	    if (!sp) {
75	      missing++
76	      mismatches.push(`${key}.${propName}: missing (rdt has it, semantic doesn't)`)
77	      continue
78	    }
79	    if (!rp) {
80	      extra++
81	      mismatches.push(`${key}.${propName}: extra (semantic has it, rdt doesn't)`)
82	      continue
83	    }
84	
85	    requiredTotal++
86	    if (rp.required === sp.required) requiredMatched++
87	    else mismatches.push(`${key}.${propName}: required rdt=${rp.required} semantic=${sp.required}`)
88	
89	    typeTotal++
90	    if (typesMatch(sp.type, rp.type)) typeMatched++
91	    else mismatches.push(`${key}.${propName}: type rdt="${rp.type}" semantic="${sp.type}"`)
92	  }
93	}
94	
95	console.log(`Components compared: ${componentsCompared}`)
96	console.log(`Props in union: ${propsUnion}`)
97	console.log(`  missing (in rdt, not semantic): ${missing}`)
98	console.log(`  extra (in semantic, not rdt):   ${extra}`)
99	console.log(`  required: ${requiredMatched}/${requiredTotal}`)
100	console.log(`  type strings: ${typeMatched}/${typeTotal}`)
101	console.log(`  descriptions: ${descriptionMatched}/${descriptionTotal}`)
102	
103	if (mismatches.length > 0) {
104	  console.log(`\n${mismatches.length} mismatches:`)
105	  for (const m of mismatches.slice(0, 50)) console.log(`  ${m}`)
106	  if (mismatches.length > 50) console.log(`  ... and ${mismatches.length - 50} more`)
107	}

1	import { API, SignatureKind, SymbolFlags, TypeFlags } from 'typescript-next/unstable/async'
2	import { SyntaxKind } from 'typescript-next/unstable/ast'
3	import { discoverFixtures, FIXTURES_ROOT } from './fixtures.ts'
4	import type { ToolResult, NormalizedProp } from './types.ts'
5	
6	const tsconfigPath = `${FIXTURES_ROOT}/../tsconfig.json`
7	
8	// Mirrors RDT 2.4.0's algorithm (lib/parser.js) via tsc --api instead of running RDT itself —
9	// see docs/type-checker-integration.md ("The algorithm"). Method names are the 7.1 client's.
10	const api = new API({ cwd: FIXTURES_ROOT })
11	const parsed = await api.parseConfigFile(tsconfigPath)
12	
13	const fixtures = discoverFixtures().filter((f) => !f.isDts) // same filter as the RDT baseline
14	const program = await api.createProgram(
15	  fixtures.map((f) => f.path),
16	  parsed.options,
17	)
18	const checker = program.project.checker
19	
20	// A component signature's first parameter is named `props`, or is the only parameter.
21	async function findComponentSignature(signatures: any[]): Promise<{ param: any } | undefined> {
22	  for (const sig of signatures) {
23	    const params = await sig.getParameters()
24	    if (params.length === 0) continue
25	    if (params.length === 1 || params[0].name === 'props') return { param: params[0] }
26	  }
27	  return undefined
28	}
29	
30	// `parent`/`declarations`: the first (resp. every) declaration's parent, when it's an
31	// interface or type alias (doc step 5). Other parents (e.g. a `cva()` object literal for a
32	// `VariantProps<...>` prop) are skipped — RDT has no equivalent for those either.
33	async function declaringTypeNames(prop: any): Promise<string[]> {
34	  const names: string[] = []
35	  for (const declHandle of prop.declarations) {
36	    const node = await declHandle.resolve()
37	    const p = node?.parent
38	    if (p && (p.kind === SyntaxKind.InterfaceDeclaration || p.kind === SyntaxKind.TypeAliasDeclaration)) {
39	      names.push(p.name.getText())
40	    }
41	  }
42	  return names
43	}
44	
45	// Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each union member's own apparent properties
46	// (doc step 3) — the checker's own apparent-properties call already narrows to the
47	// intersection of a union's members, which drops props that aren't shared across every branch.
48	async function collectProps(propsType: any): Promise<Map<string, any>> {
49	  const byName = new Map<string, any>()
50	  for (const p of await propsType.getApparentProperties()) byName.set(p.name, p)
51	  if (propsType.flags & TypeFlags.Union) {
52	    const members = (await propsType.getTypes()) ?? []
53	    for (const member of members) {
54	      for (const p of await member.getApparentProperties()) {
55	        if (!byName.has(p.name)) byName.set(p.name, p)
56	      }
57	    }
58	  }
59	  return byName
60	}
61	
62	async function normalizeProp(prop: any, location: any): Promise<NormalizedProp> {
63	  const type = await checker.getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(prop, location)
64	  const base = await checker.getBaseConstraintOfType(type)
65	  const typeStr = await checker.typeToString(base ?? type)
66	  const declarations = await declaringTypeNames(prop)
67	  return {
68	    name: prop.name,
69	    required: !(prop.flags & SymbolFlags.Optional),
70	    type: typeStr,
71	    description: await prop.getDocumentationComment(checker),
72	    parent: declarations[0],
73	    declarations: declarations.length > 0 ? declarations : undefined,
74	  }
75	}
76	
77	const results: ToolResult[] = []
78	
79	for (const fixture of fixtures) {
80	  const start = performance.now()
81	  try {
82	    const moduleSymbol = await checker.getSymbolOfSourceFile(fixture.path)
83	    if (!moduleSymbol) {
84	      results.push({
85	        tool: 'semantic',
86	        fixture: fixture.name,
87	        durationMs: performance.now() - start,
88	        output: {},
89	        error: 'no module symbol',
90	      })
91	      continue
92	    }
93	
94	    const exports = await checker.getExportsOfModule(moduleSymbol)
95	    let foundAny = false
96	
97	    for (const exp of exports) {
98	      const type = await checker.getTypeOfSymbol(exp)
99	      const callSignatures = await checker.getSignaturesOfType(type, SignatureKind.Call)
100	      let match = await findComponentSignature(callSignatures)
101	      let propsType: any
102	
103	      if (match) {
104	        const location = await match.param.valueDeclaration.resolve()
105	        propsType = await checker.getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(match.param, location)
106	      } else {
107	        // Class component: props come off the instance type's `props` member (doc step 2).
108	        const constructSignatures = await checker.getSignaturesOfType(type, SignatureKind.Construct)
109	        for (const sig of constructSignatures) {
110	          const params = await sig.getParameters()
111	          if (params.length > 1) continue
112	          const instanceType = await sig.getReturnType()
113	          const propsSymbol = await checker.getPropertyOfType(instanceType, 'props')
114	          if (!propsSymbol) continue
115	          match = { param: propsSymbol }
116	          propsType = await checker.getTypeOfSymbol(propsSymbol)
117	          break
118	        }
119	      }
120	
121	      if (!match || !propsType) continue // not a component
122	
123	      foundAny = true
124	      const location = match.param.valueDeclaration ? await match.param.valueDeclaration.resolve() : undefined
125	      const propsByName = await collectProps(propsType)
126	      const props = Object.fromEntries(
127	        await Promise.all(
128	          [...propsByName.values()].map(async (p) => [p.name, await normalizeProp(p, location)] as const),
129	        ),
130	      )
131	
132	      results.push({
133	        tool: 'semantic',
134	        fixture: `${fixture.name}/${exp.name}`,
135	        durationMs: performance.now() - start,
136	        output: {
137	          [exp.name]: {
138	            displayName: exp.name,
139	            description: await exp.getDocumentationComment(checker),
140	            props,
141	          },
142	        },
143	      })
144	    }
145	
146	    if (!foundAny) {
147	      results.push({
148	        tool: 'semantic',
149	        fixture: fixture.name,
150	        durationMs: performance.now() - start,
151	        output: {},
152	        error: 'no components found',
153	      })
154	    }
155	  } catch (error: any) {
156	    results.push({
157	      tool: 'semantic',
158	      fixture: fixture.name,
159	      durationMs: performance.now() - start,
160	      output: {},
161	      error: error.message,
162	    })
163	  }
164	}
165	
166	await program.dispose()
167	await api.close()
168	
169	console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2))

# Semantic backend (TypeScript 7)

**Status:** designed, not implemented ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md)). `PipelineOptions::resolve_complex_types` exists and does nothing. **Last verified:** 2026-09-26. Each measurement names its nightly.

## Next step

Fix the oracle first — it blocks re-verifying Accuracy and blocks committing the probe script.

1. **Fix the RDT oracle.** `apps/validate` depends on `typescript ^7.0.2`; RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` undefined — see "The RDT oracle is broken" below). Give `apps/validate`'s RDT a TypeScript 6 API: `typescript@6`, or `@typescript/typescript6` (from the 7.0 announcement), separate from the `typescript@next` build the semantic probe uses.
2. **Commit the parity probe** (the RDT-algorithm-on-`tsc --api` script under "The algorithm" and "Evidence") as a real `apps/validate` script. It currently exists only as an ad hoc scratchpad file.
3. **Re-run it against the full fixture corpus**, not just the 13 hand-picked components in "Evidence".
4. **Then** start the Rust client for the Lifecycle gate — not before, since building it against unreproducible numbers is wasted work.

Update this doc's Evidence/Gates tables and delete this section once step 3 lands.

Some props can't be resolved from the AST alone. An opt-in backend asks TypeScript's checker instead, using the algorithm react-docgen-typescript (RDT) uses, and merges the answer into the structural result. Structural extraction stays the default.

## What the structural resolver can't do

Component prop counts from `fixtures/` with `--html-attributes full`, against RDT. Root causes are from `docs/benchmarks.md`.

| Check | Result | Nightly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 13 components: the 10 outliers, base-ui `MenuRoot`, shadcn `Button`, mui `Button` | 0 missing and 0 extra props. `required` 3412/3412. Type strings 3410/3412 | 09-26 |
| Descriptions: ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 | 09-20 |
| `parent`: ariakit `MenuButton` | 294/294 in 12 requests | 09-20 |
| Fixture corpus, 55 files in one program | 70 components in common, equal prop counts on 70/70 | 09-20 |
| Class components | 2/2 on a synthetic file. The corpus has none | 09-20 |
| Full fixture corpus, 47 components / 5554 props, one program | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5265/5522. Descriptions 47/47 | 09-26 |

Type strings match after two normalizations. tsc prints union members in internal type-id order, which differs from TS 5.9, so members are compared as a set. RDT also runs `.replace(' | undefined', '')` twice, which turns a nested `=> string | undefined` into `=> string` and loses information. Canonical output keeps it. The 2 remaining differences are nested `ref` unions in fluentui and base-ui.

Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have no props and 3 are default exports RDT names differently (mui `Button` confirmed at 311/311).

The full-corpus run's 257 remaining mismatches, unlike the curated 13, aren't all real algorithm gaps:

- Most are non-component exports the "single-parameter function" heuristic sweeps in — plain string-returning helpers (`antd/buttonHelpers.ts`, `headlessui/render.ts`'s `mergeProps`, `blueprint/blueprintTypes.ts`) whose "props" are `String.prototype`/`Array.prototype` members. RDT is equally permissive and picks these up too, so both tools agree these aren't components; the mismatches are TS 6 vs TS 7.1-dev lib.d.ts differences (e.g. `padStart`'s parameter renamed `maxLength`→`targetLength`) and per-run `Symbol.iterator` id suffixes, not a resolver bug.
- `children` without a description shows as "extra" — RDT drops it, canonical keeps it (see "What gets dropped", status Done).
- One real RDT bug surfaced: `rdt-compat/svg-icon.tsx` declares two `forwardRef` components (`Icon`, `Box`) in one file; RDT resolves `Box`'s `ref` and DOM-attribute types to `Icon`'s `SVGSVGElement` instead of `Box`'s own `HTMLDivElement`. The semantic algorithm gets `Box` right — RDT is the outlier.

content.content:
156	| Accuracy against RDT | Passed on 13 components. See not verified below |
157	| Lifecycle | Not started: missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification |
158	| Cost | Measured through the Node client. Repeat with the Rust client |
159	| Determinism | Clean and incremental runs must produce the same output |
160	| Oracle | Broken. See below |
161	
162	## The RDT oracle is broken
163	
164	`apps/validate` depends on `typescript ^7.0.2`, and RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined). The baselines on disk date from 2026-07-25. RDT needs a TypeScript 6 API: `typescript@6`, or `@typescript/typescript6` from the 7.0 announcement.
165	
166	The harness also compares only name, `required`, type and default, and renders our types itself in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`). Its type mismatches mix resolver and renderer differences, and description, `parent` and `declarations` are never compared.
167	
168	## Open decisions
169	
170	1. **Output type.** Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly: `Named` has no file or symbol, `EventHandler` has no return type, `Tuple` has no optional or rest elements, and `Object` has no index signatures. Add a variant or map into existing ones. `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version, so add one first.

content.content:
1	# Semantic backend (TypeScript 7)
2	
3	**Status:** designed, not implemented ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md)). `PipelineOptions::resolve_complex_types` exists and does nothing. **Last verified:** 2026-09-27. Each measurement names its nightly.
4	
5	## Next step
6	
7	Start the Rust client for the Lifecycle gate — Accuracy is re-verified and the probe is committed, so this is no longer blocked on unreproducible numbers.
8	
9	Some props can't be resolved from the AST alone. An opt-in backend asks TypeScript's checker instead, using the algorithm react-docgen-typescript (RDT) uses, and merges the answer into the structural result. Structural extraction stays the default.
10	
11	## What the structural resolver can't do
12	
13	Component prop counts from `fixtures/` with `--html-attributes full`, against RDT. Root causes are from `docs/benchmarks.md`.
14	
15	| Gap | Example | Ours | RDT |
16	| --- | --- | --: | --: |
17	| Generics through alias chains | ariakit `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` | 5 | 294 |
18	| Generics through alias chains | ark-ui `SelectRoot` | 36 | 314 |
19	| Conditional types | headlessui `PropsOf<TTag>` | 14 | 246 |
20	| Mapped types over a generic | base-ui `WithBaseUIEvent<T>` | 11 | 293 |
21	| Conditional type and indexed access | fluentui `Slot<Type, ...>` | 8 | 303 |
22	| `@emotion/styled` two-argument overload | storybook-emotion `Button` | 7 | 306 |
23	
24	In the 2026-07-25 baseline, 10 of 33 compared components account for 2,696 of 2,720 missing props. The other 24 are `ref` and `key`, which this tool omits by design (`MIGRATING.md`).
25	
26	## How it works
27	
28	```
29	OXC parse → structural resolver ──────────────┐
30	                                              ├→ merge → ExtractionOutput
31	tsc --api → semantic resolver (opt-in) ───────┘
32	```
33	
34	The structural result is complete on its own and returns first. The semantic pass reads each exported component from the checker and replaces the structural props where it finds one.
35	
36	### Merge rules (proposed)
37	
38	| Field | Source |
39	| --- | --- |
40	| Props present, `type`, `required` | Semantic |
41	| `parent`, `declarations` | Semantic. `declarations` lists every declaring interface, not just the first |
42	| `description`, `tags` | Semantic JSDoc, structural if empty |
43	| `defaultValue` | Structural. RDT reads defaults from the AST too |
44	| Components tsc doesn't surface (not exported) | Structural only |
45	| Degrade diagnostics of a resolved component | Dropped |
46	
47	### What gets dropped, and where
48	
49	| Dropped | Where | Status |
50	| --- | --- | --- |
51	| `children` without a description | RDT projection only. Canonical keeps it | Done |
52	| Ambient `.d.ts` components such as `PureComponent` | Merge step | Done |
53	| `ref`, `key` | Not emitted, matching the structural path | Open |
54	| HTML and DOM attributes in curated and none mode | Semantic adapter, by declaring interface rather than by name | Open |
55	
56	### Delivery (proposed)
57	
58	The structural result returns immediately. The semantic result follows: the CLI waits for it behind an opt-in flag, and the NAPI binding exposes a second async call so the Vite plugin can patch when it resolves. Spawn `tsc` at the start of the run so it loads while extraction runs. Each result carries a content hash, and a stale one is dropped.
59	
60	## The algorithm
61	
62	Mirrors RDT 2.4.0 (`lib/parser.js`). Method names are from the 7.1 client.
63	
64	1. `getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)`, then `getExportsOfModule`.
65	2. For each export, `getTypeOfSymbol`, then `getSignaturesOfType(Call)`. A component has a signature whose first parameter is named `props` or is the only parameter. For a class, use `Construct` signatures and read `props` from the instance type.
66	3. Props type: `getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(param, param.valueDeclaration)`. Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each member's when it is a union.
67	4. Per prop, `type` is `typeToString(getBaseConstraintOfType(t) ?? t)` with default flags, so long types truncate as they do in RDT. `required` means the symbol lacks `Optional` and has no code default.
68	5. `parent` is the first declaration's parent when that is an interface or type alias. `declarations` is every declaration's parent.
69	6. `description` and `tags` come from `getDocumentationComment` and `getJsDocTags`.
70	
71	RDT also emits any exported symbol that has a JSDoc comment but no props. We don't. In the fixture corpus, 23 of the 26 entries only RDT emits are of this kind, such as enum members, type aliases and functions.
72	
73	## TypeScript 7.1 API
74	
75	| Topic | Detail |
76	| --- | --- |
77	| Where | `microsoft/TypeScript` `main` (`7.1.0-dev`). typescript-go closed on 2026-08-20 |
78	| Timeline | Beta 2026-10-06, RC 2026-11-10, stable 2026-11-24 ([#63703](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/63703)) |
79	| Get it | `npm i typescript@next`. 7.0.x has no API |
80	| Launch | `tsc --api --async --cwd <dir>`: JSON-RPC with LSP-style `Content-Length` framing, handled concurrently. Without `--async`: msgpack over stdio, strictly serial. `--pipe` uses a socket |
81	| Stability | JS entry points are `typescript/unstable/*`. The protocol has no version handshake, so pin the build |
82	| Positions | UTF-16 code units. OXC offsets are UTF-8 bytes |
83	| Surface | 157 methods on 2026-09-19, mostly with TS 6 checker names |
84	
85	**Churn.** About 20 commits touched the protocol definition (`proto.go`) between 2026-08-20 and 2026-09-18. `updateSnapshot`, project IDs and `createProgram` params were reshaped on 09-17 and 09-18. Every call the algorithm uses ran unchanged on the 09-20 and 09-26 nightlies. Re-verify on the beta.
86	
87	**Freshness.** tsc sees an edit to a dependency only when told:
88	
89	```js
90	const s1 = await s0.update({ fileNotifications: { changed: [file] }, ensurePrograms: true })
91	```
92	
93	With the notification, the dependent component's props updated (0.5 ms update, 2.8 ms query). An unnotified disk edit stayed stale (2026-09-20).
94	
95	## Evidence
96	
97	Method: RDT 2.4.0 on typescript@6.0.3 (`apps/validate`'s RDT is pinned to a TS6 API — see "The RDT oracle" below) with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above via `apps/validate/src/run-semantic.ts` on typescript@next. Run with `pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/validate parity`.
98	
99	| Check | Result | Nightly |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| 13 components: the 10 outliers, base-ui `MenuRoot`, shadcn `Button`, mui `Button` | 0 missing and 0 extra props. `required` 3412/3412. Type strings 3410/3412 | 09-26 |
102	| Descriptions: ariakit, MUI, fluentui, shadcn | 294/294, 311/311, 288/288, 292/292 | 09-20 |
103	| `parent`: ariakit `MenuButton` | 294/294 in 12 requests | 09-20 |
104	| Fixture corpus, 55 files in one program | 70 components in common, equal prop counts on 70/70 | 09-20 |
105	| Class components | 2/2 on a synthetic file. The corpus has none | 09-20 |
106	| Full fixture corpus, 47 components / 5554 props, one program | 5 missing, 27 extra. `required` 5508/5522. Type strings 5265/5522. Descriptions 47/47 | 09-26 |
107	
108	Type strings match after two normalizations. tsc prints union members in internal type-id order, which differs from TS 5.9, so members are compared as a set. RDT also runs `.replace(' | undefined', '')` twice, which turns a nested `=> string | undefined` into `=> string` and loses information. Canonical output keeps it. The 2 remaining differences are nested `ref` unions in fluentui and base-ui.
109	
110	Of the corpus's 26 RDT-only entries, 23 have no props and 3 are default exports RDT names differently (mui `Button` confirmed at 311/311).
111	
112	The full-corpus run's 257 remaining mismatches, unlike the curated 13, aren't all real algorithm gaps:
113	
114	- Most are non-component exports the "single-parameter function" heuristic sweeps in — plain string-returning helpers (`antd/buttonHelpers.ts`, `headlessui/render.ts`'s `mergeProps`, `blueprint/blueprintTypes.ts`) whose "props" are `String.prototype`/`Array.prototype` members. RDT is equally permissive and picks these up too, so both tools agree these aren't components; the mismatches are TS 6 vs TS 7.1-dev lib.d.ts differences (e.g. `padStart`'s parameter renamed `maxLength`→`targetLength`) and per-run `Symbol.iterator` id suffixes, not a resolver bug.
115	- `children` without a description shows as "extra" — RDT drops it, canonical keeps it (see "What gets dropped", status Done).
116	- One real RDT bug surfaced: `rdt-compat/svg-icon.tsx` declares two `forwardRef` components (`Icon`, `Box`) in one file; RDT resolves `Box`'s `ref` and DOM-attribute types to `Icon`'s `SVGSVGElement` instead of `Box`'s own `HTMLDivElement`. The semantic algorithm gets `Box` right — RDT is the outlier.
117	
118	## Cost
119	
120	Measured through the Node client on one macOS machine, so a Rust client should be lower.
121	
122	| Measure | Result |
123	| --- | --- |
124	| Spawn and first snapshot | 33–72 ms |
125	| First checker query | 1–15 ms |
126	| Request round trip | 0.1 ms. 500 positions in one request take about 1 ms |
127	| 55-file corpus, one program | 385 ms and 937 requests. RDT in-process: 955 ms |
128	| Server memory | About 100 MB (MUI `Button`) |
129	| Structural path, for comparison | 50 ms for the whole corpus, 1.75–2.1 ms per incremental update (`docs/benchmarks.md`) |
130	
131	Trimming the process, on the MUI `Button` query (median of 5 runs, 2026-09-20). Differences under about 10 ms are noise.
132	
133	| Config                                 |   Wall |    CPU | Memory |
134	| -------------------------------------- | -----: | -----: | -----: |
135	| Default                                |  85 ms | 270 ms | 102 MB |
136	| `types: []`                            |  79 ms | 260 ms | 100 MB |
137	| `types: []`, `GOGC=off`                |  71 ms | 200 ms | 111 MB |
138	| `types: []`, `GOMAXPROCS=2`            | 114 ms | 160 ms |  99 MB |
139	| Default, plus 300 unrelated root files |  88 ms | 320 ms | 112 MB |
140	
141	Pass only the files you need as roots. The API's checker is lazy, and diagnostics and emit never run.
142	
143	## Boundaries
144	
145	- **`crates/core`** owns the semantic result type, the merge and the diagnostics. It has no I/O, no async and no protocol types. The merge lives here because `OpaqueDetail` and `ParsedProp` internals are `pub(crate)`.
146	- **Backend crate** (feature-gated, off by default) spawns `tsc --api`, speaks the protocol, and handles timeouts and supervision. `config.rs` has none of these today.
147	- **CLI and NAPI** only switch it on. Neither calls JS.
148	- **Not a `DocgenPlugin`.** The hook is synchronous and runs on the cold path only. `WatchSession::update_file` skips plugins.
149	- **Failure** leaves the structural result and adds a diagnostic. It never fails extraction.
150	- **Determinism.** Reversing the query order changed no union order across 16 props in 3 files (2026-09-20). Whether canonical output sorts unions is open (below).
151
