This session already closed Accuracy (re-verified against the full 44-file fixture corpus) and Oracle (fixed RDT's TypeScript 7 incompatibility). Lifecycle — "missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification" — is listed "Not started," and the doc's own "Next step" now points here.

**Scope for this pass (confirmed with the user):** build only the process-supervisor + JSON-RPC transport crate that satisfies Lifecycle, standalone and tested against a fake `tsc`. No `crates/core` wiring, no CLI flag, no NAPI option, no real `typescript/unstable/*` checker methods — those depend on the still-open "Output type" and `ref`/`key` decisions in `type-checker-integration.md`'s "Open decisions," which are a separate follow-up once this lands.

## Approach

New workspace member `crates/tsc-client` (package `oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client`), added to root `Cargo.toml`'s `members`. No `[features]` table yet — nothing consumes it in this pass, so it just compiles as an ordinary crate; feature-gating happens when a consumer wires it in later.

Reuses two proven patterns already in this repo instead of inventing new ones:
- **Content-Length framing** — `crates/cli/src/commands/lsp.rs`'s tested design (16 MiB cap checked *before* allocating, EOF-before-header vs. no-usable-header-line treated as distinct outcomes) ported from sync std::io/server-role to async `tokio::io`/client-role. Same test scenarios, mirrored not copied.
- **Injection-safe process spawning** — `crates/cli/src/config.rs`'s node/tsx spawn (env var for paths, not shell strings; clear "is X installed?" hint on spawn failure) is the model for spawning `tsc`.

### Module layout

```
crates/tsc-client/
  Cargo.toml
  src/
    lib.rs              — public API re-exports
    error.rs             — TscClientError (thiserror), MalformedFrameReason
    protocol.rs           — JSON-RPC envelope types, RequestId
    transport/
      mod.rs
      framing.rs           — async Content-Length reader/writer (also used by fake-tsc, so client and
                              fake server can't drift on wire format)
    client.rs             — Client: request/response correlation, notifications, freshness (seq) tracking
    supervisor.rs           — Supervisor: version check, spawn, crash detection, restart policy, shutdown/reap
  tests/
    bin/fake_tsc.rs         — scenario-driven fake tsc process, a real [[bin]] (not a shell script — this
                              workspace builds on Windows CI), scenario selected via FAKE_TSC_SCENARIO env var
    common/mod.rs           — spawn_fake(scenario) test helper
    lifecycle_missing_binary.rs
    lifecycle_unsupported_version.rs
    lifecycle_timeout.rs
    lifecycle_crash.rs
    lifecycle_restart_storm.rs
    lifecycle_malformed_or_oversized_frame.rs
    lifecycle_partial_project_failure.rs
    lifecycle_shutdown_reaping.rs
    lifecycle_stale_notification.rs
```

`transport/` as a `mod.rs`-directory matches `crates/core`'s existing `extractor/`, `resolver/`, `types/`, `pipeline/` convention.

### Cargo.toml

All of `tokio` (add `"time"` feature to the existing workspace set for `timeout`/`test-util`), `serde`, `serde_json`, `camino`, `tracing`, `dashmap`, `tempfile` are **already workspace dependencies** (verified against root `Cargo.toml` and `crates/core`/`crates/cli`/`crates/binding`) — declare with `.workspace = true`. `thiserror = "2"` is the one new dependency, declared as a plain crate-local version string (not added to `[workspace.dependencies]`) — this repo already has that exact precedent for single-consumer deps (`crates/cli/Cargo.toml`'s `comfy-table = "7.0"`, `crossterm = "0.28"`). `miette` (the workspace's CLI-facing diagnostic renderer) isn't appropriate here — this is a library error type, not user-facing terminal output, and `crates/core` itself uses a plain custom type rather than miette for the same reason.

```toml
[[bin]]
name = "fake-tsc"
path = "tests/bin/fake_tsc.rs"

[dependencies]
tokio      = { workspace = true, features = ["time"] }
serde.workspace      = true
serde_json.workspace = true
camino.workspace     = true
tracing.workspace    = true
dashmap.workspace    = true
thiserror  = "2"

[dev-dependencies]
tokio      = { workspace = true, features = ["time", "test-util"] }
tempfile.workspace = true
```

**Why no `panic_guard`-style containment here:** `crates/core::panic_guard::contain_panic` exists to contain panics from caller-supplied closures on rayon/NAPI boundaries. This crate never runs an arbitrary caller closure — its only untrusted input is bytes from a child process, handled through `Result`, never `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`. State that as a deliberate decision in the crate's module doc.

### Transport: async Content-Length framing (`transport/framing.rs`)

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_BYTES: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024; // matches lsp.rs's cap

pub async fn read_frame<R>(reader: &mut R, cap: usize) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TscClientError>
where R: tokio::io::AsyncBufRead + Unpin;
// EOF before any header -> Ok(None). Header block read but no usable Content-Length,
// or truncated body -> Err(MalformedFrame) (fatal — stream position is no longer known).
// Declared length over cap -> Err(OversizedFrame), checked BEFORE allocating the buffer.

pub async fn write_frame<W>(writer: &mut W, body: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<()>
where W: tokio::io::AsyncWrite + Unpin;
```

Mirror `lsp.rs`'s existing unit tests (oversized rejected, exactly-at-cap accepted, headerless vs. true EOF distinguished, unparsable Content-Length, truncated body) as async equivalents directly in `framing.rs`, before any integration-level test exercises the same behavior through a real child process.

### Client: request/response correlation (`client.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Client(Arc<ClientInner>);

struct ClientInner {
    stdin: tokio::sync::Mutex<tokio::process::ChildStdin>,
    pending: DashMap<u64, tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<Result<TaggedResponse, TscClientError>>>,
    next_id: AtomicU64,
    next_seq: AtomicU64,                                    // wire-arrival order, for stale-notification checks
    notifications: tokio::sync::Mutex<Option<tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Notification>>>,
}

pub struct TaggedResponse { pub value: serde_json::Value, pub seq: u64 }

impl Client {
    pub async fn request(&self, method: &str, params: serde_json::Value, deadline: std::time::Duration)
        -> Result<TaggedResponse, TscClientError>;
    pub fn take_notifications(&self) -> Option<tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Notification>>;
}
```

One background task (spawned at connect) owns `ChildStdout`, loops `read_frame`, and dispatches by shape: has `id` + (`result`|`error`) → complete the matching `pending` oneshot; has `method`, no `id` → push to the notifications channel; unparsable body → log and drop (recoverable — a malformed *body* doesn't desync the stream, only a malformed *header* does). A single `fail_all_pending(err)` path (called on crash or fatal framing error) drains `pending` and closes the notifications channel.

### Supervisor: one decision per Lifecycle item (`supervisor.rs`)

- **Missing binary** — `tokio::process::Command::new(tsc_path).spawn()` failing → `SpawnFailed { path, source }` with a config.rs-style "install `typescript@next` or pass an explicit path" hint. No retry.
- **Unsupported version** — read `tsc_path`'s adjacent `package.json` `"version"` field *before spawning* (no protocol round trip, no process cost for a doomed launch) and compare against a compiled-in pinned allowlist. Mismatch → `UnsupportedVersion`; unreadable/unparsable → `VersionCheckFailed`.
- **Timeout** — `request()` takes an explicit `deadline: Duration` (no crate-wide default; Cost table shows call cost ranges from ~1ms to ~400ms) and wraps the oneshot await in `tokio::time::timeout`. Only the internal handshake gets a built-in constant (`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT = 10s` against a measured 33–72ms). On elapse: remove the pending entry (a late response becomes a no-op send) and return `Timeout { method, after }`.
- **Crash** — two signals converge on one `fail_all_pending`: a dedicated task awaits `child.wait()` once; the reader task's own loop hits EOF/IO error. Whichever fires first wins; the other is a no-op (oneshots already completed).
- **Restart storm** — bounded: `MAX_RESTARTS = 3` within `RESTART_WINDOW = 60s`, backoff `200ms → 400ms → 800ms` (capped `5s`). Exceeding the cap moves the `Supervisor` to a terminal failed state; every later call short-circuits with `RestartStormDetected` without touching the process again.
- **Malformed/oversized frame** — malformed **header** is fatal (byte offset of the next frame is unrecoverable) and routes through `fail_all_pending`; malformed **JSON body** (Content-Length was valid) is recoverable — log and drop that one frame. Oversized is fatal, checked pre-allocation, cap configurable (`SupervisorConfig::max_frame_bytes`, default `DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_BYTES`) so tests don't need to push 16 MiB over a pipe.
- **Partial project failure** — no batching/aggregation in this crate: `request()` is per-call. A well-formed JSON-RPC `error` response scopes to that one request (`RpcError { code, message, data }`) and never touches a concurrently in-flight sibling — that per-call/session-wide error distinction (`RpcError` vs. `Crashed`/`RestartStormDetected`) is what a future merge step needs to tell "this component failed" from "the whole run failed."
- **Shutdown reaping** — `pub async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<(), TscClientError>`: mark shutting-down first (so the crash-watcher doesn't misreport a clean exit), drop `ChildStdin` (EOF), race a 2s grace `child.wait()`, `kill()` on timeout, then **unconditionally** `wait()` again so the child is always reaped. `Drop` is a non-blocking best-effort `start_kill()` + `tracing::warn!` fallback only — the real guarantee lives in `.shutdown()`.
- **Stale notification** — `next_seq` stamps every inbound frame in true wire-arrival order (not issue order, not wall clock); `TaggedResponse.seq` lets a caller mechanically check "could this answer reflect an update I already got acked?" (`answer.seq > update_ack.seq`) without needing the real (still-churning) `updateSnapshot` wire shape.

**One refinement on top of this design:** a bare `Client` handle is tied to one child process's `ClientInner` — after a Supervisor-driven restart, old `Client` clones held by a caller are permanently `SessionClosed`. Give `Supervisor` its own `pub async fn request(...)` that fetches the current `Client`, and on `Crashed` (with restart budget remaining) restarts once and retries the same call once before propagating; `Supervisor::client()` stays available for a caller that wants the low-level handle without that retry behavior.

```rust
pub struct SupervisorConfig {
    pub tsc_path: camino::Utf8PathBuf,
    pub cwd: camino::Utf8PathBuf,
    pub handshake_timeout: std::time::Duration,  // default 10s
    pub max_frame_bytes: usize,                  // default DEFAULT_MAX_FRAME_BYTES
}

impl Supervisor {
    pub async fn spawn(config: SupervisorConfig) -> Result<Self, TscClientError>;
    pub fn client(&self) -> Client;
    pub async fn request(&self, method: &str, params: serde_json::Value, deadline: std::time::Duration)
        -> Result<TaggedResponse, TscClientError>;   // restart-on-crash, retried once
    pub async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<(), TscClientError>;
}
```

### Error type (`error.rs`)

One `thiserror`-derived enum, one variant family per Lifecycle item so a test can assert on which failure mode fired: `SpawnFailed`, `UnsupportedVersion`, `VersionCheckFailed`, `Timeout`, `Crashed`, `RestartStormDetected`, `OversizedFrame`, `MalformedFrame(MalformedFrameReason)`, `RpcError`, `SessionClosed`, `Write`.

### Fake-tsc test harness (`tests/bin/fake_tsc.rs`)

A real tokio `[[bin]]`, not a shell script (this workspace builds on Windows CI — confirmed via `Cargo.lock`'s Windows target entries). Scenario picked via `FAKE_TSC_SCENARIO` env var (env-over-argv, matching `config.rs`'s precedent for test/caller-controlled input): `never_respond`, `hang_after_n:<N>`, `exit_after:<N>:<code>`, `garbage_bytes`, `bad_content_length`, `oversized_frame:<N>`, `truncated_body`, `echo` (baseline; honors `params.fail` to emit an `error` object), `reorder_ack` (answers request 2 before request 1), `shutdown_slow:<ms>`.

Built against this crate's own `transport::{read_frame, write_frame}` for every "valid frame" scenario so the fake server can't drift from what the real client parses; "bad frame" scenarios intentionally hand-write raw bytes instead.

One test file per Lifecycle item, each spawning `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-tsc")` through a shared `tests/common/mod.rs` helper and asserting on the specific `TscClientError` variant (or, for shutdown reaping: wall-clock bound + process no longer alive; for stale notification: `seq` ordering).

### Explicitly not built this pass

No `crates/core` wiring, no CLI flag, no NAPI option, no `[features]` gate (nothing consumes this crate yet), no real `typescript/unstable/*` methods (`getSymbolOfSourceFile`, `getExportsOfModule`, real `updateSnapshot`/`fileNotifications` shape, etc.) beyond the fake harness's own synthetic `echo`. No resolution of `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` — `tsc_path` is caller-supplied. A future consumer plugs in via `Supervisor::request("typescript/unstable/...", json!({...}), deadline)` with no transport/supervisor redesign needed.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client` — unit tests in `framing.rs` (mirrored from `lsp.rs`'s cases) plus one integration test per Lifecycle item (9 files) against `fake-tsc`, all green.
- `cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client -- -D warnings` clean, `unsafe_code = "deny"` satisfied (inherited via `[lints] workspace = true`).
- Manual smoke check against the real thing: `npm i -g typescript@next` (or reuse `apps/validate`'s already-resolved `typescript-next` install), point `SupervisorConfig::tsc_path` at its `bin/tsc`, confirm `Supervisor::spawn` + one raw `request("initialize", ...)` round-trips against the real 7.1 nightly — not a `cargo test`, a one-off run to confirm the fake harness's assumptions about wire behavior (framing, exit codes) match reality before this becomes load-bearing for the real algorithm later.
- `cargo build --workspace` still succeeds with the new member added to root `Cargo.toml`.

### Critical files

- `crates/tsc-client/Cargo.toml` — new
- `crates/tsc-client/src/transport/framing.rs` — new, mirrors `crates/cli/src/commands/lsp.rs`
- `crates/tsc-client/src/client.rs` — new
- `crates/tsc-client/src/supervisor.rs` — new
- `crates/tsc-client/tests/bin/fake_tsc.rs` — new
- `Cargo.toml` (root) — add `crates/tsc-client` to `[workspace] members`
- `crates/cli/src/commands/lsp.rs` — read for the framing pattern being ported, not modified
- `crates/cli/src/config.rs` — read for the spawn-safety pattern being ported, not modified

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

[workspace.dependencies]

oxc_allocator     = "0.151"
oxc_parser        = "0.151"

oxc_ast_visit     = "0.151"
oxc_span          = "0.151"

trycmd            = "1.2"

[profile.release]

use std::time::Duration;

use camino::Utf8PathBuf;

/// One variant family per Lifecycle-gate item (docs/type-checker-integration.md,
/// "Gates before it ships") so a caller or test can tell failure modes apart.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum TscClientError {
    #[error("tsc binary not found at {path} — install `typescript@next` (npm i typescript@next) or pass an explicit path ({source})")]
    SpawnFailed { path: Utf8PathBuf, #[source] source: std::io::Error },

    #[error("tsc at {path} reports version {found:?}, not pinned (expected one of {expected:?})")]
    UnsupportedVersion { path: Utf8PathBuf, found: String, expected: &'static [&'static str] },

    #[error("could not determine tsc's version at {path}: {reason}")]
    VersionCheckFailed { path: Utf8PathBuf, reason: String },

    #[error("request {method:?} timed out after {after:?}")]
    Timeout { method: String, after: Duration },

    #[error("tsc exited unexpectedly (status: {status:?})")]
    Crashed { status: Option<std::process::ExitStatus> },

    #[error("tsc restarted {attempts} times within {window:?}; treating as permanently failed")]
    RestartStormDetected { attempts: u32, window: Duration },

    #[error("oversized frame: declared Content-Length {declared} exceeds the {cap}-byte cap")]
    OversizedFrame { declared: usize, cap: usize },

    #[error("malformed frame: {reason:?}")]
    MalformedFrame { reason: MalformedFrameReason },

    #[error("tsc returned a JSON-RPC error (code {code}): {message}")]
    RpcError { code: i64, message: String, data: Option<serde_json::Value> },

    #[error("session already shut down or permanently failed")]
    SessionClosed,

    #[error("I/O error writing to tsc: {0}")]
    Write(#[source] std::io::Error),

    #[error("failed to serialize a request: {0}")]
    Serialize(#[source] serde_json::Error),
}

/// A malformed **header** desyncs the stream (the next frame's byte offset becomes
/// unknowable) and is always fatal for the session. A malformed **body** is scoped to
/// one frame — the declared length was valid, so the reader can resync on the next
/// frame — and the caller decides whether that's fatal for its use case.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MalformedFrameReason {
    NoContentLengthHeader,
    UnparsableContentLength,
    TruncatedBody,
    InvalidJson,
}

use camino::Utf8PathBuf;

/// One variant family per Lifecycle-gate item (docs/type-checker-integration.md,
/// "Gates before it ships") so a caller or test can tell failure modes apart.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum TscClientError {
    #[error("tsc binary not found at {path} — install `typescript@next` (npm i typescript@next) or pass an explicit path ({source})")]
    SpawnFailed { path: Utf8PathBuf, #[source] source: std::io::Error },

    #[error("tsc at {path} reports version {found:?}, not pinned (expected one of {expected:?})")]
    UnsupportedVersion { path: Utf8PathBuf, found: String, expected: &'static [&'static str] },

    #[error("could not determine tsc's version at {path}: {reason}")]
    VersionCheckFailed { path: Utf8PathBuf, reason: String },

    #[error("request {method:?} timed out after {after:?}")]
    Timeout { method: String, after: Duration },

    #[error("tsc exited unexpectedly (status: {status:?})")]
    Crashed { status: Option<std::process::ExitStatus> },

    #[error("tsc restarted {attempts} times within {window:?}; treating as permanently failed")]
    RestartStormDetected { attempts: u32, window: Duration },

    #[error("oversized frame: declared Content-Length {declared} exceeds the {cap}-byte cap")]
    OversizedFrame { declared: usize, cap: usize },

    #[error("malformed frame: {reason:?}")]
    MalformedFrame { reason: MalformedFrameReason },

    #[error("tsc returned a JSON-RPC error (code {code}): {message}")]
    RpcError { code: i64, message: String, data: Option<serde_json::Value> },

    #[error("session already shut down or permanently failed")]
    SessionClosed,

    #[error("I/O error writing to tsc: {0}")]
    Write(#[source] std::io::Error),

    #[error("failed to serialize a request: {0}")]
    Serialize(#[source] serde_json::Error),

    #[error("failed to reap tsc's process: {0}")]
    Reap(#[source] std::io::Error),
}

/// A malformed **header** desyncs the stream (the next frame's byte offset becomes
/// unknowable) and is always fatal for the session. A malformed **body** is scoped to
/// one frame — the declared length was valid, so the reader can resync on the next
/// frame — and the caller decides whether that's fatal for its use case.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MalformedFrameReason {
    NoContentLengthHeader,
    UnparsableContentLength,
    TruncatedBody,
    InvalidJson,
}

content.text:
The `crates/tsc-client` crate is done and fully verified. Summary:

**Built:** a standalone Rust crate (`oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client`) implementing the process supervisor + async JSON-RPC/Content-Length client for `tsc --api --async`, satisfying every item in the Lifecycle gate — missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed/oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification. One integration test per item (plus a couple extra), all against a real scenario-driven `fake-tsc` test binary, no shell scripts (Windows-CI-safe).

**Verified:**
- `cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client` — 23/23 passing
- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `cargo deny check` — clean (no new advisory/license/ban issues)
- `cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi` — clean
- **Real-world smoke test**: spawned the actual `typescript@next` 7.1.0-dev nightly (already resolved in `apps/validate`), sent a live `initialize` request over the real wire protocol, got a correctly-parsed response, shut down cleanly. Added as `cargo run -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client --example smoke_real_tsc` for future manual re-verification.

One deviation from the approved plan worth flagging: I dropped the "two converging crash signals" design (a separate `child.wait()` watcher task alongside the reader task) — it would've created a `Child` ownership conflict with the supervisor's own restart/shutdown logic. The reader task's EOF detection alone is a reliable, race-free signal, so that's the sole crash-detection path now.

Nothing else changed outside the new crate (`Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` only gained the new workspace member). Ready to commit — want me to?

content.text:
Mostly, but there are a few real gaps — not disasters, but places where I chose simplicity/consistency-with-the-repo over the more idiomatic async-Rust path:

**1. Hand-rolled framing instead of `tokio_util::codec`.** My `read_frame`/`write_frame` functions manually loop over `AsyncBufRead`/`AsyncWrite`. The more idiomatic approach in the tokio ecosystem is implementing `tokio_util::codec::{Decoder, Encoder}` and wrapping the child's stdio in `Framed`, giving you a `Stream`/`Sink` that composes with `StreamExt`/`SinkExt` combinators instead of a bespoke async fn pair. This is how `tokio-tungstenite`, `tower-lsp`, and most serious framed-protocol crates do it. I mirrored `crates/cli/src/commands/lsp.rs`'s existing sync style instead, for consistency with the repo precedent — a real trade-off, not an accident, but the codec route is genuinely more idiomatic.

**2. The `SessionEnd` type is a code smell.** I invented a parallel `Copy` enum purely because `TscClientError` can't derive `Clone` (it wraps `io::Error`), and I needed to fan one failure out to every pending waiter. The idiomatic fix: wrap the `io::Error` sources in `Arc<io::Error>` (or use `Arc<TscClientError>` at the call boundary), making the error itself cheaply cloneable and deleting `SessionEnd` entirely. This is the one I'd actually go fix.

**3. Untyped `serde_json::Value` API.** `Client::request` takes/returns raw `Value` instead of `request<P: Serialize, R: DeserializeOwned>`. This was a deliberate scope call (the plan explicitly deferred typed checker-method wrappers to a later pass), not an idiom miss — but it's why the API feels raw today.

Everything else — `Arc<Inner>` newtype for cheap-clone handles, `oneshot` + `DashMap<id, Sender>` for request correlation, `thiserror` for the error enum, `unreachable!()` for internal invariants instead of `.expect()` — is standard, idiomatic async-Rust service architecture.

Want me to fix #2 now (cheap, contained) and/or #1 (bigger, touches `transport/framing.rs` and `client.rs`'s reader loop)?

# oxc-react-docgen

10-100x faster than react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.

# Memory Index

- [No Claude attribution](feedback_no_coauthor.md) — No Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session trailers, or session links in PRs
- [Concise writing](feedback_concise_writing.md) — no AI slop/wordy prose in comments, docs, specs; see docs/adr/README.md's banned-words list

use std::time::Duration;

use camino::Utf8PathBuf;

/// One variant family per Lifecycle-gate item (docs/type-checker-integration.md,
/// "Gates before it ships") so a caller or test can tell failure modes apart.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum TscClientError {
    #[error("tsc binary not found at {path} — install `typescript@next` (npm i typescript@next) or pass an explicit path ({source})")]
    SpawnFailed {
        path: Utf8PathBuf,
        #[source]
        source: std::io::Error,
    },

    #[error("tsc at {path} reports version {found:?}, not pinned (expected one of {expected:?})")]
    UnsupportedVersion { path: Utf8PathBuf, found: String, expected: &'static [&'static str] },

    #[error("could not determine tsc's version at {path}: {reason}")]
    VersionCheckFailed { path: Utf8PathBuf, reason: String },

    #[error("request {method:?} timed out after {after:?}")]
    Timeout { method: String, after: Duration },

    #[error("tsc exited unexpectedly (status: {status:?})")]
    Crashed { status: Option<std::process::ExitStatus> },

    #[error("tsc restarted {attempts} times within {window:?}; treating as permanently failed")]
    RestartStormDetected { attempts: u32, window: Duration },

    #[error("oversized frame: declared Content-Length {declared} exceeds the {cap}-byte cap")]
    OversizedFrame { declared: usize, cap: usize },

    #[error("malformed frame: {reason:?}")]
    MalformedFrame { reason: MalformedFrameReason },

    #[error("tsc returned a JSON-RPC error (code {code}): {message}")]
    RpcError { code: i64, message: String, data: Option<serde_json::Value> },

    #[error("session already shut down or permanently failed")]
    SessionClosed,

    #[error("I/O error writing to tsc: {0}")]
    Write(#[source] std::io::Error),

    #[error("failed to serialize a request: {0}")]
    Serialize(#[source] serde_json::Error),

    #[error("failed to reap tsc's process: {0}")]
    Reap(#[source] std::io::Error),
}

/// A malformed **header** desyncs the stream (the next frame's byte offset becomes
/// unknowable) and is always fatal for the session. A malformed **body** is scoped to
/// one frame — the declared length was valid, so the reader can resync on the next
/// frame — and the caller decides whether that's fatal for its use case.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum MalformedFrameReason {
    NoContentLengthHeader,
    UnparsableContentLength,
    TruncatedBody,
    InvalidJson,
}

content.text:
Both fixes are in and everything passes: 11 unit tests, all the lifecycle integration tests, clippy (workspace-wide), `cargo deny`, and the smoke run against the real TypeScript 7.1 nightly.

**#2, cloneable error:**
- `TscClientError` is now `Clone`. The `io::Error` and `serde_json::Error` sources are wrapped in `Arc`, so a clone is just a refcount bump.
- `SessionEnd` is deleted, and `fail_all_pending` clones the error to each waiter.
- The reader loop no longer needs the `unreachable!()` guard, since any error variant can be broadcast.

**#1, `tokio_util::codec`:**
- Framing is now a `ContentLengthDecoder` (a `Decoder`) read through `FramedRead`. `Client`'s reader task and `fake-tsc` both use the same decoder, so they can't drift on wire format.
- `write_frame` stays a plain async function: a frame is always fully formed before it's sent, so an `Encoder`/`Sink` would add ceremony for no gain.

- Read-side I/O errors used to be folded into "looks like EOF". `Decoder` requires `Error: From<io::Error>`, so they now surface as a `Read` variant. That was a side benefit I hadn't planned.

New dependencies: `tokio-util` (codec), `tokio-stream`, `bytes`. I used `tokio-stream` rather than the full `futures` crate to keep the footprint small.

A diff spanning multiple independent topics — common on a backlog/catch-up run, not just a single PR — produces one changeset per topic, not one bundled entry. When the change came via smith, pass along implementer's criteria_evidence — changeset-analyzer uses those exact locations instead of reconstructing approximate ones from the diff.
- courier:commit: Trigger when the user asks to commit code or write a commit message: "commit this", "write a commit message", "commit the staged changes". Reads the staged git diff and produces a conventional commit message explaining why the change was made, not what changed — the diff already shows what changed.
- courier:post-review: Trigger when the user has an already-drafted review or reply and wants it posted: "post this review", "reply to this comment", "mark this thread resolved", "submit my review comments". Takes drafted content — from the built-in `code-review` skill's findings, from `courier/receive-feedback`'s response plan, or typed directly by the user — and posts it to GitHub via `gh pr review` or `gh pr comment`. Does not draft content itself; this skill is purely mechanical execution of something already written, gated by explicit user confirmation before any post fires.
- courier:pr: Trigger when the user asks to open a PR or write a PR description: "open a PR", "create a pull request", "write the PR description". Given a diff, a linked spec, and a linked requirement, produces a PR title and body a reviewer with zero context can act on, then opens the PR via `gh pr create` after user confirmation.
- courier:receive-feedback: Trigger when the user asks to process or triage incoming review feedback: "address the feedback", "respond to review comments", "what do these comments mean", "triage this review". Assembles a review package — diff summary, linked spec, test results, open questions — so the author has full context to respond without re-reading the whole thread. Does not categorize individual comments by priority; that's the caller's judgment call, made with `shared/references/delivery/github.md`'s vocabulary in hand. This is for feedback received on the user's own PR — critiquing someone else's PR is the built-in `code-review` skill's job, not this one.
- courier:release: Trigger when the user asks to cut a release or summarize what's in one: "cut a release", "what's in this release", "generate release notes". Aggregates changeset@2 entries since the last release into a release-artifact@2: filters consumer_impact: internal-only entries, computes the version as max(semver_impact) across the rest applied to the prior version, and carries each changeset's summary through unedited.
- muse:component: Trigger when the user asks to spec a UI component: "spec this component", "draft a component spec", "write a spec for this design", "audit this component spec", "is this component spec ready?", "gate this component spec". Given a requirement@1 or free-text design intent, produces a spec@1 covering props, variants, per-state observable behavior, and accessibility criteria as testable propositions. Every criterion is falsifiable from outside the implementation; error cases and invalid prop combinations carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead. Gated by a binding exit gate before the spec proceeds to planning.
- navigator:plan: Trigger this skill when the user says "write a plan for X", "how do we implement this spec", "break this down into tasks", "what are the implementation steps", "create an implementation plan", or "plan this out". Also activate when a spec (spec@1) exists and the user is ready to move to implementation but hasn't broken it down yet. Produces a plan@1 artifact where every task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code, the exact tests proving each criterion, a conventional commit message, and covers_criteria linking the task to specific acceptance criteria. spec_file_path and linked_requirement are propagated from the source spec. No TBDs. No "implement as appropriate." Every step is mechanically executable by a developer with zero domain context.
- ranger:audit: Find evidence-backed reachable defects in Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Refute candidates, group defect families, and verify fixes against current code and the relevant execution boundary.
- scribe:architect: Trigger when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Produce the smallest `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable through a type, API, boundary, invariant, lint, test, or CI rule.
- scribe:audit-architecture: Trigger when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture — not another spec, and not a single signature — before it reaches scribe/gate-spec: "check this spec against our architecture", "does this fit the system", "audit this against the arch model". Given a spec@1, checks it against the persisted arch-model@2 for boundary violations, competing abstractions, and invariant conflicts, building or refreshing the model first if it's absent or stale for the area the spec touches. Returns specific, rewritten fixes on fail, the same standard as scribe/audit-spec but at system scope instead of spec scope.
- scribe:audit-spec: Trigger when the user asks to review a spec's quality: "review this spec", "is this spec complete?", "audit this spec". Given a spec@1, adversarially reviews it for untestable criteria, ambiguous language, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, and incomplete sections. Returns a structured issue list with specific rewritten suggested fixes, not generic guidance. Named audit-spec rather than audit because the bare word audit is already ranger's plugin-level skill name (code/bug auditing) — a different domain entirely.
- scribe:correct-spec: Trigger when implementer reports that a spec criterion contradicts what the system actually does: a spec_contradiction status from smith. Use this when implementation reveals the spec itself is wrong, not merely hard to satisfy.
- scribe:draft-spec: Trigger when the user asks to write or draft a spec: "spec this out", "draft a spec", "write a spec for this requirement". Given a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1, produces a spec@1 draft with purpose, scope, non_goals, api_surface (if applicable), and acceptance criteria. Every criterion is a testable proposition; error cases carry is_error_case: true. No TBDs anywhere in the document — genuinely unknown items go in non_goals or the reasoning scratchpad instead.
- scribe:gate-spec: Trigger when a spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before it enters planning: "gate this spec", "is this spec ready?", "check this spec before we plan it". Default disposition is fail — the spec must earn a pass. Passes only if every acceptance criterion is testable with no vague language, no TBDs remain, error cases are explicitly covered, and scope is narrow enough for one planning cycle. This gate checks the spec on its own terms — whole-system architectural fit is scribe/audit-architecture's job upstream, not re-litigated here. On fail, returns blockers specific enough for scribe/draft-spec to act on without further clarification.
- scribe:spec-drift: Trigger when the user asks whether implemented code still matches its spec, weeks or months after implementation: "check spec drift", "does the code still match this spec?", "has this spec drifted?". Given a spec@1 (via spec_file_path) and a workspace root, reads the spec from disk and the implementation from the workspace, and reports each criterion as covered (implemented and tested), uncovered (no matching implementation), or drifted (implementation exists but diverges from the criterion's contract). - scribe:verify-spec: Trigger when the user asks whether a spec matches its source: "is this grounded?", "does this spec match the requirement?", "check this spec against the requirement". # Ranger — Cross-Language Bug Hunting

## Modes

- Full sweep: scan every hazard taxonomy.
- Targeted scan: scan the named category.
- Candidate verification: send the supplied candidate directly to adversary.
- Post-remediation check: run exit-gate against prior findings.

## Pipeline

```text
workspace → recon → scanner → [boundary-tracer] → adversary → finding-report@2 → exit-gate
```

1. `recon` records live files, entry points, languages, capabilities, workspace state, and workflow provenance in `workspace-manifest@1`.
2. `scanner` loads the matching hazard reference and emits `candidate@1` without judgment.
3. `boundary-tracer` produces `field-survival-map@1` for T7 and T10 candidates.
4. `adversary` emits `candidate-assessment@1` for one candidate. It confirms only a reachable failing scenario; external uncertainty produces `plausible`.
5. The caller aggregates findings and their families into `finding-report@2`.
6. After remediation, `exit-gate` independently derives sibling candidates and verifies current code with project-native evidence. It emits `verdict@3`.

## Defect-family route

Treat confirmed findings with the same root cause, domain responsibility, or failure state as one possible defect family. Search beyond copied syntax: equivalent behavior may use different names, control flow, or language.

When a family suggests a missing concept, state, operation, boundary, abstraction, invariant, or enforcement mechanism, pass the complete `finding-report@2` to `scribe:architect` before remediation. Local or unrelated findings remain ordinary remediation work.

## Verification depth

Choose evidence by risk, not language ritual. Use the project-native test, mutation, property, fuzz, race, integration, or boundary tools that can discriminate the suspected defect. A property or fuzz check needs a meaningful generator and oracle. Record unsupported or impractical checks as coverage gaps; do not imply coverage.

## Dispatch

| Agent | Mode | Tier | Input → output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `recon` | Enumeration | haiku / low | workspace → `workspace-manifest@1` |
| `scanner` | Pattern matching | sonnet / medium | manifest → `candidate@1` |
| `boundary-tracer` | Data-flow tracing | sonnet / medium | T7/T10 candidate → `field-survival-map@1` |
| `adversary` | Adversarial judgment | opus / high | one candidate → `candidate-assessment@1` |
| `exit-gate` | Binding verification | opus / high | `finding-report@2` → `verdict@3` |

## Contracts

- Candidates: `shared/schemas/candidate@1.json`
- Candidate assessment: `shared/schemas/candidate-assessment@1.json`
- Workspace: `shared/schemas/workspace-manifest@1.json`
- Boundary evidence: `shared/schemas/field-survival-map@1.json`
- Findings: `shared/schemas/finding-report@2.json`
- Exit verdict: `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`

Plausible findings pass to `flagged_for_review`; they never become remediation blockers without confirmation.

(4) `Client::take_notifications` uses `try_lock().ok()?` on an async mutex: can it return None spuriously when the lock is contended even though notifications were never taken? The write-path adversary confirmed two high-severity defects, both from one root cause (C015 and C074), each reproduced with a throwaway test through the public API:

- **Cancellation desync:** dropping a `Client::request` future mid-write leaves a partial frame on stdin. After that, every request on every `Client` clone times out, and `is_alive()` still returns `true`.
- **Deadline ignored on write:** a child that stops reading stdin blocks the write past the deadline while it holds the stdin mutex, and every other request queues behind it.
- **Proposed fix:** a dedicated writer task that owns `ChildStdin` and receives whole frames over a channel.

The other five adversaries are still running.

The response-correlation adversary is back with two confirmed medium-severity defects, one dismissed candidate, and three plausible ones.

**Confirmed:**
- **Requests after a dead reader (C006/C013):** `ClientInner` has no closed flag. A request issued after the reader exits on a fatal frame error is inserted into `pending` and nothing ever resolves it. It costs a full deadline and reports `Timeout` instead of the frame error. The fix is a closed state that the reader sets before it drains, and that `request()` checks after inserting.
- **Shutdown strands in-flight requests (C011):** `shutdown()` aborts the reader before it drains `pending`. An in-flight request on a `Client` clone waits out its whole deadline (4s in the test).

**Dismissed (C016):** a late response can never reach another caller, because request ids are unique.

**Plausible, depends on what real tsc sends:**
- **C005:** a well-framed body that isn't valid JSON or doesn't match the response shape is only logged, and the caller times out.
- **C020:** a `null`, string or non-u64 id, or a reply with no `result`, is dropped and the caller times out.
- **C021:** a message with both `id` and `method` becomes a notification and its `id` is lost.

**Side finding:** `SessionClosed` is effectively unreachable, so the doc on `Supervisor::client` promises an error callers never get.

The shutdown adversary confirmed two defects, rated one more plausible at medium, and dismissed the rest. It ran against the real 7.1.0-dev nightly as well as fake-tsc.

**Confirmed, medium (C054, same root cause as C011):** `shutdown()` aborts the reader task before it drains `pending`. With the real tsc, a request in flight on a `Client` clone returned `Timeout` after its full 30s deadline, even though `shutdown()` itself returned in 0.7ms.

**Confirmed, low (C055):** `shutdown()` drops only the Supervisor's `Arc`. If a caller still holds a `supervisor.client()` clone, stdin never closes, so tsc never sees EOF.
- **Cost:** shutdown always waits the full 2s grace period and then force-kills. The measured times are 1.26ms with no clone held and 2.003s with one held.
- **Reaping:** still guaranteed.
- **Fix:** make stdin closable from the supervisor.

**Plausible, medium (C030):** the stderr drain stops on the first read error, and a non-UTF-8 line counts as one. That drops the pipe, and tsc dies of SIGPIPE on its next stderr write. It reproduced with a stand-in child. It only matters if real tsc ever prints non-UTF-8 bytes to stderr.

**Plausible, low (C058):** if node is old enough that `bin/tsc` doesn't `execve`, only the node wrapper gets killed and the native tsc is orphaned. On this node (v26.3.0) the child is the native binary.

**Test gap:** `shutdown_force_kills_and_reaps_a_process_that_ignores_it` never reaches the force-kill branch. The fake exits on stdin EOF, so shutdown finishes in about 107ms. That branch only runs when the test holds a `Client` clone.

**Dismissed:** the `start_kill`, `kill_on_drop`, stderr-task-leak and `unreachable!` candidates.

Two adversaries are still running: restart bookkeeping and dead config.

# finding-report: crates/tsc-client (2026-09-28, ranger:audit, 99 candidates -> 6 adversary clusters)

Crate: crates/tsc-client (standalone, unconsumed, uncommitted). Contract under audit: Lifecycle gate in docs/type-checker-integration.md ("missing binary, unsupported version, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, partial project failure, shutdown reaping, stale notification"). All evidence below was reproduced by adversaries (throwaway tests, fake-tsc, /bin/sh stubs, and the real typescript@next 7.1.0-dev.20260926.1); throwaway files were deleted.

## Family A — a session has no terminal state (structural)
Root cause: `ClientInner` has no closed/terminal state. The reader task drains `pending` exactly once on its natural exit; nothing marks the session closed, `request()` never checks, `shutdown()` aborts the reader before it drains, and `Supervisor::request` decides to restart only from the current call's error (Crashed|Write), never from whether the session's reader ended.
- CONFIRMED medium C006/C013 (client.rs:66,:139,:121): request after reader exit inserts into `pending`, never resolved -> full-deadline `Timeout` naming the wrong cause (garbage_bytes: 3.0037s).
- CONFIRMED medium C011/C054 (supervisor.rs:211 + client.rs:121): `shutdown()` aborts reader, `fail_all_pending` skipped; in-flight request on a Client clone waits its whole deadline (real tsc: shutdown 0.7ms, request 30.0s -> Timeout).
- CONFIRMED medium NEW-1 (supervisor.rs:171): OversizedFrame/MalformedFrame(header)/Read ends the reader while the child stays alive; Supervisor never restarts, storm cap never trips, every later request Timeouts (4/4 at 300ms, is_alive=false, spawns=1). `is_alive()` detects it, nothing calls it.
- CONFIRMED low C-crashed-status (client.rs:118): `Crashed.status` always None; exit status is discarded in restart (supervisor.rs:198) and shutdown (:215).
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C005 (client.rs:54): well-framed but non-JSON/mis-shaped body only warn!-logged, waiter Timeouts; `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson` never constructed.
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C020/C021 (protocol.rs:58,:62): null/non-u64 id or `{"id":1}` with no result dropped -> Timeout; id+method frame misfiled as Notification. Real pinned tsc sends neither (0 notifications observed).
- Doc defect: `Supervisor::client` doc promises `SessionClosed` for stale clones; in practice Write/Crashed/Timeout (SessionClosed effectively unreachable).

## Family B — the write path is not owned by the session (structural)
Root cause: any caller's future performs a multi-poll `write_frame` while holding the shared stdin mutex, and `deadline` wraps only the response `rx`. Also stdin lives inside `ClientInner`, so only dropping every Client clone closes it.
- CONFIRMED high C015/C074 (client.rs:150-158, framing.rs:124): dropping a `Client::request` future mid-write (select!/timeout) leaves a partial frame on the pipe; every later request on every clone then Timeouts, `is_alive()` stays true, no Crashed/Write, never restarted (8 MiB body, echo fake: 3/3 later pings Timeout ~502ms).
- CONFIRMED medium C-stdin-lock-deadline (client.rs:151): child that stops reading stdin -> write blocks past `deadline` holding the mutex; other requests queue behind it (1 MiB/100ms deadline still blocked at 2s; 4 KiB frames: request 15 blocks once the ~64 KiB pipe fills).
- CONFIRMED low C055/C056 (supervisor.rs:212): with any `supervisor.client()` clone held, stdin never closes, so tsc (which exits on stdin EOF: 1.26ms without clone) always takes the 2s grace + SIGKILL (2.003s). Reaping still guaranteed.
- Note: framing.rs module doc claim "a frame is always fully formed before it's sent ... no partial-state problem" is false under cancellation.

## Family C — untrusted child output is not bounded (local fixes)
- PLAUSIBLE medium C061/C059/C069 (framing.rs:51,:93): no header-size cap; no `\r\n\r\n` grows the buffer without bound and rescans from offset 0 each decode (real FramedRead over `yes`: 84 MB in 10.6s; 128 MiB direct decode 42.7s, quadratic). Real pinned tsc emits only `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n` on stdout, so not confirmed.
- PLAUSIBLE medium C030 (supervisor.rs:81): stderr drain `while let Ok(Some(..))` stops on first read error (non-UTF-8 line), drops the pipe, tsc dies of SIGPIPE on next stderr write -> silent crash/restart (reproduced with a stand-in child).
- PLAUSIBLE low C063 (framing.rs:61): header name matched case-sensitively with exactly one space; real tsc emits exactly `Content-Length: %d`.
- PLAUSIBLE low C058 (supervisor.rs:219): on Node without `process.execve` (or Windows) `bin/tsc` falls back to execFileSync -> native tsc becomes a grandchild that start_kill/kill_on_drop do not kill.
- Hardening note C008 (client.rs:96): unbounded notification channel; pinned tsc sent 0 notifications -> dismissed for the pinned build.

## Family D — declared but unenforced contract (mixed)
- CONFIRMED low C-handshake (supervisor.rs:31): `SupervisorConfig.handshake_timeout` (default 10s) is never read; a tsc that starts but never becomes ready is never detected or restarted (spawn Ok in 285us, request Timeouts, no restart). Real nightly answers `initialize` in ms.
- CONFIRMED low C038 (supervisor.rs:128): `failed` is terminal forever; after 3 restarts in 60s (e.g. UnsupportedVersion after `npm i typescript@next`) every call is RestartStormDetected even after the cause is fixed; message says "restarted 3 times" although no restart succeeded and hides the root cause.
- PLAUSIBLE medium C041 (supervisor.rs:173): after restart the request is replayed unchanged into a fresh tsc with no session setup (`{"snapshot":1,"symbol":42}` replayed into process 3 returned Ok); TaggedResponse.seq restarts at 1, so fresh answers compare as stale under `answer.seq > update_ack.seq`. Depends on how real tsc treats per-run IDs.
- Cleanup: `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson` dead variant; `saw_header_line` dead branch in `parse_content_length`; `Ordering::SeqCst` stronger than needed.
- Test gap: `shutdown_force_kills_and_reaps_a_process_that_ignores_it` never reaches the force-kill branch (fake exits on stdin EOF; 107ms) — it only runs when a Client clone is held.

## Dismissed (with evidence; do not re-litigate)
C016 late-response misattribution (ids unique), C057/C031/C029/C033-C035 (start_kill, kill_on_drop, stderr task leak, unreachable! after Stdio::piped), C060/C067 (decoder state after error: reader breaks on first Err, FramedRead returns None), C064/C065 (`+2` and duplicate Content-Length cause no misframing on a one-parser pipe), C072/C073 (partial header at EOF correctly mapped to Crashed), C047/C049-C053 (backoff/cap arithmetic, restart cleanup, old reader isolation), `take_notifications` try_lock (30x16-thread contention: exactly one Some).

## Invisible invariants (no machine enforcement)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable 1 (no `unwrap()` outside #[cfg(test)]): workspace clippy is `all = warn` only; `unwrap_used`/`expect_used` not enabled. tsc-client complies today by convention.
- Non-negotiable 6 (always emit Diagnostic when degrading): convention only; client.rs:54 degrades a bad frame to `warn!` with no signal to the caller.
- crates/core/AGENTS.md panic-containment rule: convention only.

## Family routing
Families A and B share one missing concept: a session that owns its I/O (a writer task that owns stdin and receives whole frames, a reader task, and an explicit closed-with-reason state that request(), shutdown() and the Supervisor all observe). -> scribe:architect. Families C and D are ordinary remediation except C038/C041, which need a small design decision (recovery semantics, replay policy).

## Family A — a session has no terminal state (structural)
Root cause: `ClientInner` has no closed/terminal state. The reader task drains `pending` exactly once on its natural exit; nothing marks the session closed, `request()` never checks, `shutdown()` aborts the reader before it drains, and `Supervisor::request` decides to restart only from the current call's error (Crashed|Write), never from whether the session's reader ended.
- CONFIRMED medium C006/C013 (client.rs:66,:139,:121): request after reader exit inserts into `pending`, never resolved -> full-deadline `Timeout` naming the wrong cause (garbage_bytes: 3.0037s).
- CONFIRMED medium C011/C054 (supervisor.rs:211 + client.rs:121): `shutdown()` aborts reader, `fail_all_pending` skipped; in-flight request on a Client clone waits its whole deadline (real tsc: shutdown 0.7ms, request 30.0s -> Timeout).
- CONFIRMED medium NEW-1 (supervisor.rs:171): OversizedFrame/MalformedFrame(header)/Read ends the reader while the child stays alive; Supervisor never restarts, storm cap never trips, every later request Timeouts (4/4 at 300ms, is_alive=false, spawns=1). `is_alive()` detects it, nothing calls it.
- CONFIRMED low C-crashed-status (client.rs:118): `Crashed.status` always None; exit status is discarded in restart (supervisor.rs:198) and shutdown (:215).
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C005 (client.rs:54): well-framed but non-JSON/mis-shaped body only warn!-logged, waiter Timeouts; `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson` never constructed.
- PLAUSIBLE low-med C020/C021 (protocol.rs:58,:62): null/non-u64 id or `{"id":1}` with no result dropped -> Timeout; id+method frame misfiled as Notification. Real pinned tsc sends neither (0 notifications observed).
- Doc defect: `Supervisor::client` doc promises `SessionClosed` for stale clones; in practice Write/Crashed/Timeout (SessionClosed effectively unreachable).

## Family B — the write path is not owned by the session (structural)
Root cause: any caller's future performs a multi-poll `write_frame` while holding the shared stdin mutex, and `deadline` wraps only the response `rx`. Also stdin lives inside `ClientInner`, so only dropping every Client clone closes it.

- CONFIRMED low C055/C056 (supervisor.rs:212): with any `supervisor.client()` clone held, stdin never closes, so tsc (which exits on stdin EOF: 1.26ms without clone) always takes the 2s grace + SIGKILL (2.003s). Reaping still guaranteed.

content.text:
The audit is finished, and I've handed the structural findings to the architect.

**What the audit found in `crates/tsc-client`:** 9 confirmed defects, 7 plausible, and about 40 dismissed with evidence. The full report is at `scratchpad/finding-report.md`. Most of it comes from two root causes, both structural:

- **A, a session has no terminal state.** Requests made after the reader dies, and requests in flight during shutdown, wait out their whole deadline and report `Timeout`. A fatal frame error while the child stays alive is never restarted.
- **B, the write path isn't owned by the session.**
  - **Cancellation:** dropping a `request` future mid-write leaves a partial frame that wedges every clone. This is the one high-severity finding.
  - **Deadlines:** the deadline doesn't cover the write.
  - **Shutdown:** stdin can't be closed while clones exist, so shutdown always takes 2s.

`scribe:architect` is now drafting the smallest spec that makes recurrence impossible. The shape it's evaluating: a session that owns a writer task and a reader task, plus an explicit closed-with-reason state that every caller observes.

**The rest is ordinary fixes, not part of that spec:**
- **Header-size cap in the decoder:** the header can grow without bound.
- **Stderr drain:** it stops on a non-UTF-8 line and drops the pipe.
- **`handshake_timeout`:** it's never read.
- **`failed` flag:** the restart-storm flag never resets.
- **Restart replay:** a restarted request replays into a fresh session unchanged.
- **Node fallback:** on a Node without `execve`, tsc runs as a grandchild that the kill doesn't reach.

**The crate is not committed yet.** I'd hold the commit until the spec's fix lands. The alternative is to commit now as a known-defective first cut and fix it in a follow-up on a stacked PR. Tell me which you prefer once the spec is back.

content.text:
The spec is back: `SPEC-TSC-CLIENT-001`, with 15 falsifiable acceptance criteria. Each confirmed finding maps to a failing test that has to pass. It's saved at `scratchpad/spec-session-owns-io.json`.

Its main decisions:
- **No new `Session` type.** `ClientInner` becomes the session owner: a writer task alone holds `ChildStdin` and is fed whole frames over a bounded channel.
- **Compile-time enforcement.** Nothing else can write to the pipe, because the handle is moved into the task.
- **One closed state.** It is set once, with a reason. `request()`, `shutdown()` and the Supervisor all read it.
- **New restart rule.** The Supervisor restarts on any closed session, not just `Crashed | Write`. This removes NEW-1 by construction.
- **`shutdown()` returns the reaped exit status.** That also covers the `Crashed.status` gap.

The architect also says this warrants a short ADR (0007). The boundary is easy to revert without knowing why, because a task plus channel looks heavier than a mutex.

It left five design questions with defaults already written into the criteria. I'll ask the three that change behavior, plus what to do about committing.

questions.question: On shutdown, what happens to requests still in flight?

options.label: Fail immediately (Recommended)
options.description: In-flight requests get SessionClosed the moment shutdown starts. Deterministic, and real tsc exits on stdin EOF in about 1 ms anyway.

options.label: Let them land first
options.description: Wait up to the 2s grace period for responses before failing the rest. Friendlier to slow queries, but shutdown latency becomes unbounded by the caller's own deadlines.

questions.question: A child that always sends a bad header now burns the 3-restart budget in 3 calls. Restart on every kind of session end?

options.label: Yes, restart on any (Recommended)
options.description: Simple rule with no exceptions: a closed session is restarted, and the storm cap bounds a misbehaving child. This is what removes the never-restarts bug (NEW-1).

options.label: Not for frame errors
options.description: Treat MalformedFrame/OversizedFrame as non-restartable and return them immediately. A frame error usually means a real tsc bug or version mismatch, so restarting rarely helps, but every caller then handles a second failure mode.

questions.question: Where should the write-queue size (16 whole frames) live?

options.label: A const (Recommended)
options.description: Fixed bounded queue of 16 frames. Nothing to tune until a real consumer exists.

options.label: A SupervisorConfig field
options.description: Callers can tune it now. More API surface to keep stable before any consumer needs it.

questions.question: Should I commit the crate now as a known-defective first cut, or hold the commit until the spec's fix is done?

options.description: Implement the spec, re-run the audit's reproducing tests, then commit one clean crate. No defective code enters history.

options.label: Commit now, fix on a stacked PR
options.description: Land the current crate first, then the fix as a second PR using gh stack. The history shows the defects and the fix separately, but the first PR is knowingly wrong.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/.claude/plugins/cache/orin-dx-agent-plugins/smith/2.4.4/skills/implement

# Smith — Implementation Skill

<capability>
Smith executes cohesive subsystem batches. Workspace discovery records languages and available capabilities; implementation selects evidence from changed risks; review checks verification and defect families; the exit gate limits its verdict to observed scope.
</capability>

<io>
**Consumes**: `plan@1` or `spec@1` when no plan exists.

**Produces**: committed code when authorized, `workspace-manifest@1`, `implementation-result@1`, `mutation-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, and `verdict@3`.

The caller aggregates `criteria_evidence` for exit-gate and later passes it with the diff to `courier:changeset`.
</io>

<implementation_cycle>
For each subsystem batch, read persisted criteria, implement the smallest safe solution, and choose verification from `shared/references/verification/evidence.md` plus capabilities in `workspace-manifest@1`. Record exact commands, observations, boundaries, and criterion locations in `implementation-result@1`. Commit only with explicit authorization.
</implementation_cycle>

<mutation_gate>
Use project-native mutation tooling when available and relevant. A safe deliberate fault may provide equivalent discrimination evidence. Return meaningful survivors as precision tests; record unavailable evidence as a gap in `mutation-report@2`.
</mutation_gate>

<review_gate>
After discrimination testing, `reviewer` produces `implementation-review@2` using `shared/schemas/implementation-review@2.json`. It judges verification fit and records positive or negative evidence for both sibling-search modes.

Review each changed defect as a possible family. The review must cover:

- Syntactic siblings with the same code shape or algorithm.
- Semantic siblings with the same domain responsibility or failure state.
- Candidate sites supporting semantic completeness, including zero-match claims.
- The shared root cause for related instances.
- Missing concepts, states, operations, boundaries, abstractions, invariants, or enforcement.
- Boundary reach, input-space method, relevant environments, external-state freshness, and coverage gaps.
- One disposition: fix instances, unify implementation, escalate architecture, or explicitly defer.

Route the result:

- `approved` → continue.
- `changes_requested` → return must-fix issues and unresolved families to `implementer`, then repeat mutation and review.
- `needs_architecture` → halt the batch and route the review to `scribe:architect`. Gate the resulting spec, amend and challenge the plan, then resume Smith.
</review_gate>

<exit_gate>
After every planned batch has a terminal result and approved review, `exit-gate` reads persisted artifacts and current code independently. It challenges semantic completeness, verifies current state and dispositions, and emits scoped `verdict@3` using `shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`.
</exit_gate>

<subagent_dispatch_matrix>
| Agent | Role | Tier | Delegate when |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `recon` | Workspace manifest | haiku / low | Before edits: record state, languages, capabilities, baseline, and drift. |
| `implementer` | Batch implementation | sonnet / medium | Implement and test one subsystem batch. |
| `mutator` | Mutation gate | sonnet / medium | Test whether changed behavior is meaningfully covered. |
| `reviewer` | Pre-gate analysis | sonnet / medium | Inspect scope, quality, and defect families after mutation. |
| `exit-gate` | Binding verification | opus / high | Verify the complete changeset after all reviews pass. |
</subagent_dispatch_matrix>

<context_management>
Pass only the current batch, recon manifest, persisted paths, current precision tests, and authorization state to `implementer`. Track each planned batch and started verification task until it has a terminal result; unresolved work reaches exit-gate as `pending_checks`.
</context_management>

<recovery>
- `needs_context`: resolve the named missing file or baseline state before retrying.
- `spec_contradiction`: halt remaining work; route the evidence to `scribe:correct-spec`, then amend and challenge the plan. Escalate if the same criterion contradicts twice.
- Implementer `needs_architecture`: route the complete `implementation-result@1` to `scribe:architect`, then gate, amend, and challenge before resuming.
- Reviewer `needs_architecture`: route the complete `implementation-review@2` to `scribe:architect` so the structural spec retains every family instance and assessment.
</recovery>

Skip N-5 (untouched attribute line), N-7 (Notify vs CancellationToken) and S-4 (overlaps deferred replay policy, Family D).

Then rerun: cargo fmt -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client; cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-tsc-client at least 4 times (report any flake with the failing assertion text); the smoke example. # 0007. A session owns its child's I/O and closes once, with a reason

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-09-28

## Context

`crates/tsc-client` is the Rust client for `tsc --api` (ADR 0006). Its first cut let any caller's `request()` future write to the child's stdin under a shared mutex, and nothing recorded that a session had ended. An audit against the Lifecycle gate in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` reproduced six failures from that one cause:

- Dropping a request future mid-write left a partial frame on the pipe. Every later request on every `Client` clone timed out, and `is_alive()` stayed `true`.
- A child that stopped reading stdin blocked a write past its deadline and queued every other caller behind the mutex.
- A request made after the reader exited, or in flight during `shutdown()`, waited out its whole deadline and reported `Timeout`.
- A fatal frame error from a child that stayed alive was never restarted, because the supervisor only matched `Crashed | Write`.
- Stdin closed only when every `Client` clone dropped, so shutdown always spent the 2 s grace period and then sent SIGKILL.

Patching each one leaves the cause in place: no one owned the pipe, and no state said the session was over.

## Decision

A session owns its I/O and ends exactly once.

- **One writer.** A writer task alone holds `ChildStdin`. Callers send whole frames over a bounded channel (`WRITE_QUEUE_FRAMES = 16`), so a dropped request future has enqueued a full frame or nothing.
- **One close.** A set-once closed state carries the reason. Reader exit, a write failure and `Supervisor::shutdown` all set it. Setting it fails every pending waiter and stops the writer, which drops stdin even while `Client` clones are alive.
- **One deadline.** `request()` puts enqueue and response under a single deadline and fails at once when the session is closed.
- **Restarts follow state.** The supervisor decides restarts from the closed state only. It never matches error variants or polls task handles. Shutdown closes the session first, then reaps the child and returns its exit status.

## Consequences

- A task and a channel replace a mutex. That is the point: the mutex version is what the audit broke.
- The queue is bounded in frames, not bytes. Sixteen 8 MiB frames can hold 128 MiB.
- Any close reason triggers a restart. A child that always sends a bad header burns the three-restart budget in three calls, and the storm cap then stops it.
- A `Client` clone from before a restart fails at once with its own session's reason, not a generic error.
- Each task holds a guard that closes the session on drop, so a panicking task cannot leave a session open.
- A cancelled `Supervisor::request` can burn one restart attempt.
- Enforced by tests: `dropping_a_request_future_mid_write_never_wedges_the_session`, `a_child_that_stops_reading_stdin_cannot_hold_a_request_past_its_deadline`, `shutdown_wakes_requests_blocked_on_a_full_write_queue`, `shutdown_fails_in_flight_requests_on_clones_with_session_closed` and `a_fatal_frame_from_a_live_child_is_restarted_not_timed_out`. `ChildStdin` is moved into the writer task and sits in no struct field, so no other code can write to the pipe.

## Alternatives considered

- **Patch each instance** (a liveness check per call, a stdin timeout, abort the reader after draining). Each patch leaves the shared cause, and the next instance is one edit away.
- **Keep the mutex, add a write timeout.** A timed-out `write_all` still leaves a partial frame that desyncs tsc's decoder.
- **Unbounded queue.** Memory grows without limit against a child that stops reading.

# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

lines: - [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.

- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.

+- [7. A session owns its child's I/O and closes once, with a reason](0007-session-owns-child-io.md) — do not let a caller's future write to the child's stdin, and do not decide restarts by matching error variants.
Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

input.command:
git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(tsc-client): add the Rust client and process supervisor for tsc --api

ADR 0006's semantic backend needs a client that survives a misbehaving tsc. This crate covers the Lifecycle gate (missing binary, version pin, timeout, crash, restart storm, malformed or oversized frame, shutdown reaping, stale answers), tested against a fake tsc and the real 7.1 nightly. It is standalone: nothing consumes it yet.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3; git log --oneline -1; git add docs/adr/0007-session-owns-child-io.md docs/adr/README.md docs/type-checker-integration.md && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs(adr): record why a session owns its child's I/O and closes once

The audit of crates/tsc-client traced six Lifecycle failures to one missing boundary, and a task plus a channel where a mutex would do is easy to revert without that context. Updates the Lifecycle row in the type-checker doc to match.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3; git log --oneline -3; git status --short
